Kanté came off the bench and made it 5-0, a lovely rising finish after being sent clear by Solomon, then the Israel international completed the rout with a deflected shot via a post.

Sports.title: Premier League news: Iraola values Wirtz’s work ethic; Moyes backs ‘senior citizen’ Grealish
Sports.content:
1. Wirtz’s worth ‘not all about statistics’ Andoni Iraola has insisted Florian Wirtz should be judged by his influence on Liverpool rather than statistics and believes the player’s impact will increase as his rapport with a new-look attack develops. Wirtz impressed in Liverpool’s defeat of Atlético Madrid on Wednesday, having also produced some of his best performances last season in the Champions League. But he has also come in for criticism this season for the amount of times he has conceded possession. The £116m Germany international has one assist and no goals in the Premier League so far. “Flo played very well against Atlético Madrid and I also think he has been unlucky,” said Iraola. “I remember the ‘goal’ he scored against Nottingham Forest; they gave it live and then VAR disallowed it. He could have had very good assists but we haven’t finished them. That is why you cannot just play because of the numbers. “Whether a striker scores a lot of goals or he doesn’t, you have to look at the performances. Does he help us to play well? Yes. Well, someone will score the goals and someone will give the assists. I am not too focused on numbers. Nowadays everything is about numbers, everyone tells players you have to assist, you have to score goals. For me, you have to help us play well. Someone will score the goals and I don’t care if it is the midfielders like it was the other day. Someone will score the goals if we are doing well collectively. “There is an argument to make that the wingers have changed more than anywhere else,” Iraola said. “Now we have new weapons we can use with Bradley and Victor. With Florian, he is key for us. I am not worried because he will quickly learn where Victor prefers the ball or where Bradley prefers the ball. And, also, Bradley in just his second game you could see they already had a good association. I am not very worried.” Andy Hunter

2. Grealish ‘can be a wingers’ role model’ David Moyes has told Jack Grealish he wants him to become a role model at Everton for fellow wingers Tyrique George and Tyler Dibling. Grealish made an immediate impact from the bench against Manchester United last Sunday in his first outing since rejoining Everton on loan from Manchester City. Despite a lack of minutes in pre-season, as he recovered from the fractured foot that curtailed his first campaign with Everton, the 31-year-old could start for Moyes’s side at Tottenham on Saturday. The Everton manager wants Grealish to take on more responsibility this season. “Jack knows when he comes here there is an opportunity for him to play and to show what he can do,” Moyes said. “But I also want him to be a senior professional and a role model. We’ve got Tyrique and Tyler and if ever you are looking at somebody for how to play as a wide player, Jack Grealish would certainly be one of them. “I think both of them could learn an awful lot from Jack and I want him to become that senior citizen among them, somebody who teaches them. We’ve got a mature Jack Grealish now as well in terms of understanding the game and being a team player – not that he is an individual but he plays with an individual style.” Moyes believes there is greater expectation on Grealish given it is his second season at the club and there is a need to fill the creative gap created by Iliman Ndiaye’s departure. “If there is one person who would be able to carry that it would be Jack, just because of the way he is,” he added. View image in fullscreen Jack Grealish made an immediate impact from the bench against Manchester United last Sunday in his first outing since rejoining Everton on loan. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA “He’s had six and a half months out. He’s had no pre-season games, he came on for 15 minutes in the Community Shield, so he’s had no real football and Jack is someone who thrives on the football. He gets himself fit through the games more so than the training. We need to be careful and see how he goes but he’s looking good.” Andy Hunter

3. João Pedro ‘as good as Haaland’, says Alonso Xabi Alonso has claimed João Pedro is at Erling Haaland’s level and similar in style to Karim Benzema. The Chelsea striker has reacted to missing out on Brazil’s World Cup squad by making an excellent start to the season and was named the Premier League’s player of the month on Friday. João Pedro has scored twice in his first three league appearances and has formed an exciting attacking trio with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers. Chelsea have scored 16 goals in all competitions and Alonso did not hold back when asked if the 24-year-old is as good as Haaland. “I would say yes,” Chelsea’s manager said. “If you count how many top strikers we have in the Premier League, I’m sure that João is there. Haaland for sure is there. So I would rate him that way.” The range of João Pedro’s game has added to his threat. Alonso played with Benzema at Real Madrid and sees similarities between the pair. “In many things he reminds me of Benzema,” he said. “He is good in the box, he is good out of the box, he is good coming to his left side, he is good with the head, he is very complete, he is intelligent. Still young, still things to develop, but many, many absolutely outstanding qualities.” Chelsea host Hull on Saturday afternoon and will be looking for a strong home performances after fighting back from 2-0 down to beat Leeds 6-3 in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday. View image in fullscreen João Pedro has scored twice in his first three league appearances for Chelsea. Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters Palmer was key to the comeback and revealed that Alonso, who had rotated heavily, ripped into his players at half-time against Leeds. “I was angry with myself that I didn’t help the players to play better or have a better feeling,” Alonso said. “There is a moment that you try to explain what is not working well, try to make preparations and then there is a moment that you need to kick their arse a little bit, in a nice way. It worked – not for me but the players who came on with a better quality and better everything in the second half.” Chelsea will again be without Moisés Caicedo. The midfielder is yet to start this season and Alonso does not want to risk him. Jacob Steinberg

Sports.title: Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall: ‘I’ve seen all of the meltdowns and it annoyed me’
Sports.content:
Transfer deadline day may be “exciting for everyone”, as Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall puts it, but his experience of that transfer deadline day at Everton hauled him through the same gamut of emotions as every Evertonian. Excitement turned to bewilderment before the conclusion of the window left the midfielder exasperated, but for entirely different reasons to a fanbase left questioning the club’s direction under The Friedkin Group.

How, now, is the mood in the squad? It is the obvious place to start after a deadline day that left David Moyes with fewer players than he had at the beginning, one striker and no cover for either full-back position. It also featured the US international striker Folarin Balogun walking out on a £40m transfer minutes after submitting a deal sheet. “Really good to be honest,” Dewsbury-Hall insists. “Definitely not the same mood as what I’ve seen on the outside. There’s a good mentality this year of: ‘We’ll show everyone.’” Everton’s performances so far this season support that view.

“I’ve seen all of the reactions, all of the meltdowns, and in all honestly it annoyed me a bit,” Dewsbury-Hall says in forthright and insightful fashion. “I get where people are coming from; everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad. But there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded.

“I saw people saying: ‘We’ll be lucky to stay up this year.’ What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go – and that’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room. Of course we would have wanted to sign a couple more, but we’re happy with what we’ve got and it’s given us more impetus now to move on.”

Moyes has expressed concern over the signals Everton’s transfer business could send to the dressing room at a time when he is trying to push the team on. So has it had a detrimental impact? “Not really, no,” Dewsbury-Hall insists. “I know we’ve got a smaller squad but we’ve got some really good players. Our starting XI is top, a European starting XI.

View image in fullscreen Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall says he needed his move to Everton to avoid his career stagnating. Photograph: Tony McArdle/Everton FC/Getty Images

“I get it, you need a whole squad, but we’ve got 17, 18 players at a really, really good level. I don’t think a couple of years ago it was at that level. Actually I know it wasn’t. Things can be out of your hands in football and that’s what happened for us. But we quickly realised: ‘Hang on a minute, look around the dressing room – top player, top player, top player.’ If we’re doing the right things we can still be successful.”

Dewsbury-Hall will be crucial to those prospects. The midfielder has flourished since his £28m arrival from Chelsea last summer, his game-time and growing influence vindicating the decision to leave Stamford Bridge behind. “I’m in the prime years of my career,” he says. “I couldn’t afford to spend more years stagnating.” The 28-year-old’s influence extends behind the scenes. This summer, following Séamus Coleman’s departure, he was nominated for a new leadership group that was established to compensate for the loss of the long-serving Everton captain.

“Because Séamus has left such a big hole we need a group of experienced lads to crack on together and keep the standards high and to drive things,” Dewsbury-Hall explains. “It’s just the more experienced lads – [Jordan] Pickford, Tarky [James Tarkowski, the new club captain], Jimmy [James] Garner, myself. The ones that have been playing in the Premier League for years or feel like they are settled at the club.

View image in fullscreen Kiernan Dewsbury Hall lets fly in Everton’s impressive 2-2 draw with Manchester United. Photograph: Tony McArdle/Everton FC/Getty Images

“It’s nice [to be voted in after just one season] but it’s definitely an impact I wanted to have. I’m really pleased that the lads look at me as someone that can be important for the dressing room.”

That sense of responsibility is evident in Dewsbury-Hall’s mentoring of fellow midfielder Harrison Armstrong, the 19-year-old who almost joined Nottingham Forest before deadline day only for the furious response of Evertonians at Bournemouth to prompt a U-turn from the club’s owners. “They definitely made their feelings known and obviously it worked,” says Dewsbury-Hall. “Big credit to them for that, they were amazing that day. And I know for a fact it made Harrison feel very good and it helped him. He is a very confident lad and well respected in the dressing room for such a young age.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“If there is anything I can help him with then I will. Shooting’s definitely one because his shooting is sometimes not the best, and I’ve told him that many times. But he’s got pretty much everything else. He always likes to say he’s got a better strike than me so I just tell him to look at the [Crystal] Palace goal [that Dewsbury-Hall scored on the opening day] or the Wolves goal last season. We have good banter.”

The Nottingham-born midfielder is clear in his targets for this season: European qualification, which he contends can be achieved despite the smaller squad, a strong cup run, improvement in his all-round game and a first England call-up. His rising performance levels have not gone unnoticed by Thomas Tuchel, who names his squad next Friday.

Dewsbury-Hall says: “I know I’m the closest I have ever been now. You get a message two weeks before the squad is announced. I got one for the long list for the World Cup and I’ve had one for these next games. It’s nice. It means you are doing OK. It’s a long, long message. It tells you that it’s a legal requirement for us [the Football Association] to tell you in advance that you are in contention and to be available for these dates. It’s a good feeling because you think: ‘OK, I am close,’ but you know you have to keep pushing it to the last minute. It’s up to me. It’s got to be me that forces his hand to choose me. It’s not going to be given to me.”

Nor will anything be given to Everton, but Dewsbury-Hall and company will push on regardless.

Sports.title: Under-fire Russell Martin hits out at 'personal' attacks following Leicester City's dire results - and opens up on 'difficult' period for loved ones amid widespread criticism: 'I don't know why I upset so many people'
Sports.content:
Leicester City manager Russell Martin said that he feels criticism he has received has 'become really personal' as he opened up on a turbulent start to the season with the League One side.

Leicester were tipped by many to come straight back up to the Championship after suffering back-to-back relegations from the Premier League to League One.

Yet they sit 18th in the third division after their opening five games, with Martin's side notching just one win, two draws and two defeats to leave them at their lowest ever position in the 142-year history of the club.

The Foxes were thrashed 4-0 at home to Oxford United last weekend, leaving Martin's job under intense scrutiny as he faced chants of 'sacked in the morning' from both the travelling and home fans.

In the lead-up to Leicester's match against Stockport on Saturday, Martin - who is married to former glamour model Lucy Pinder - opened up on the criticism and the toll it's taken on his loved ones, saying: 'It has become really personal from some guys in the media and definitely from fans.

'It is what it is, and I have to deal with it. It doesn't affect me too much, genuinely, but it is really difficult for the people around me, who know me and understand me and know what I am.

Martin said: 'I don't know why I upset so many people. One of the players asked me this week why I am so criticised outside of here, because obviously they see stuff, and I can't answer it'

The Leicester boss said the onslaught has been difficult for his loved ones. He is married to former glamour model Lucy Pinder

'I don't know why I upset so many people. One of the players asked me this week why I am so criticised outside of here, because obviously they see stuff, and I can't answer it.'

Martin has been working to implement a possession-heavy style, which is already turning off many fans, while former Foxes forward Matt Piper described it as 'passing teams to death'.

The 40-year-old manager still appears to have the backing of his players, however. Captain Harry Souttar claimed after last weekend's Oxford defeat that it was 'solely' the responsibility of the players.

And 20-year-old defender Jayden Joseph said the squad believes in Martin's philosophy, urging patience from the club's fanbase. 'We need to give it that bit of time for it all to come together,' he said.

Martin said on Friday: 'Speak to the players and people I've worked with, and (then) people who have never seen it and have maybe watched a few clips of some bits, and it's a very different perception from reality.

'But I guess when you try to do something that is a bit different to some, then it's always there to be shot at.'

He also doubled down on his playing style, adding: 'I love what I do, I love my job and love always trying to develop people and players by playing in a way where I think they can bring the best version of themselves.

'Sometimes it takes time. It's not easy, but I will always choose to try to embark on something that I really believe in that focuses on trying to develop whilst winning. And maybe I'm in the wrong job for that.

The Foxes were thrashed 4-0 at home to Oxford United last weekend, leaving Martin's job under intense scrutiny as he faced chants of 'sacked in the morning' from both sets of fans

'There is enough feeling from me and the players I work with that it can be really brilliant at times.

'I always have to keep learning and I spent a long time out of the game after Rangers and spent a lot of time watching different football and trying to sharpen my tools.

'The most frustrating thing is that I've enjoyed the process here so much so far and it's not quite shown with the results, but I'm convinced it will. Otherwise, I wouldn't do it. So ultimately I'll keep doing what I'm doing and hopefully we will be really successful and I really believe we can be.'

Since guiding Southampton to the Premier League via the 2023-24 Championship play-offs, Martin has won only three of his last 28 league matches across two years with three different clubs (Southampton, Rangers and Leicester) for an 11 per cent win ratio.

His time at Scottish giants Rangers saw him win just one of his seven league matches, drawing five and losing the other. Across 17 games in all competitions there, he recorded just five victories.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia was banned for racial slurs, hit with a $1m doping fine and U-turned on his support for Donald Trump... but America's controversial rock-and-roll boxer is out to save his sport by beating Britain's Conor Benn
Sports.content:
A dazzling talent just reaching his prime will enter the T-Mobile Arena here this Saturday night with the hopes of a fighting nation resting on his shoulders. Conor Benn, not so much. British boxing is enjoying a boom, not least with its dominance in the marquee heavyweight division. The young man the son of Nigel is challenging for the world welterweight crown carries the burden of restoring America to its historic pre-eminence in the prize-ring. Not just by adding to an unusually low head count of their champions but by resuscitating the excitement, the stardust, the impudence, the controversy, the brilliance and the fascination of the public over here with the hardest game of all. Ryan Garcia is the only poster boy left to them following the retirement of Floyd Mayweather. Vitally, he has all it takes to bring a new generation of fans clamouring to his fights. At 28 he has the matinee idol looks of a young Elvis Presley which brings the girls squealing into the crowds. A rock and roll bad-boy reputation which chimes with the lads. Showmanship within the ring and charisma outside the ropes. Ryan Garcia will take on Conor Benn on Saturday night with the American carrying the hopes of a fighting nation on his shoulders Garcia has reconciled with Andrea Celina Velarde (left), the beautiful mother of two of his three children (above) Benn has arrived in Las Vegas with the aim of taking the WBC welterweight belt from Garcia Glamorous blondes vie for his favours. Even though he is resisting those temptations now he has scrapped divorce proceedings and reconciled with Andrea Celina Velarde, the beautiful mother of two of his three children. And, boy, can he box. The speed of hand and foot. The knock-out punching power. The taunting evasion. And, yes, the conceit which on occasion gets him into trouble. The two defeats scarring his 28-fight record – against two of America’s other world champions Gervonta Davis and Rolly Romero – came when he was at his most arrogant and complacent. The no-decision verdict which negated his stand-out victory over Devin Haney was imposed for failing a post-fight drug test for performance-enhancing Ostarine. Like Benn he protested his innocence: ‘I’ve never knowingly taken drugs.’ His relatives revealed he had been struggling with his mental health and against alcohol. But unlike Conor he preferred taking his punishment – a $1million fine and a 12-month ban – rather than financing a protracted court case which would also have kept him under lengthy suspension. Not that King Ry - he wears a gold crown for his ring entrances - is prone to compromising his regally unvarnished opinions. Garcia was a vociferous backer of Donald Trump in his first presidential election campaign. But given his Mexican roots he criticised Trump’s second-term deportation policy. Finally he renounced his support, denouncing the Trump administration’s handling of the Epstein Files. A devout Christian, he called rapper Eminem a satanist and posted on Twitter: ’I don’t support the LGBTQ+. F*** you guys. Rot in hell.’ He called for a boycott of the Olympics for ‘disrespecting Jesus Christ' with the section of the opening ceremony of France 2024 in which drag queens imitating Greek gods were widely supposed to be parodying the Last Supper. Garcia scrapped divorce proceedings with influencer Andrea in August 2025 Garcia turned down WBC offers to help with his mental health difficulties but progress has been deemed to be made, leading to him fighting and beating Mario Barris in February The rock-and-roller came out in him when he was arrested for causing $150,000- worth of damage while trashing a room and a corridor at the ritzy Waldorf Astoria hotel in Beverly Hills. That risked a short prison term, which has not been applied. Another suspension was imposed. This one from competing in fights sanctioned by the WBC for racist slurs live on the internet against the black community and muslims. President Mauricio Sulaiman reported that Garcia had turned down a number of offers from the WBC to help Garcia with his mental health difficulties. Sulaiman relented last November, saying he recognised the progress made in that regard by the fighter’s large family. Promptly, this February, Garcia defeated the highly rated Mario Barrios to claim the WBC welterweight belt, inflicting a first round knockdown on his way to a unanimous decision. The braggadocio bubbles to the surface before fights. As soon as this weekend’s bout was announced he told Benn to his face: ‘You box like amateur trash. You're just a flashy trash can. I’m going to throw you out with trash.’ All the ingredients are there for the making of a turbulent, troubled super-star son of this angry and violent 21st century. All wrapped up in the rare skills and brave heart of a potentially great fighter. Some indication of whether all that will be enough for him to kindle another golden age in US boxing may be seen in how he deals with Benn. The huge scale of that task is evident in this, my overwhelmingly American list of the 20 greatest boxers of all time, with Lennox Lewis the Brit who came closest to inclusion...

Sports.title: Former Man United boss Ruben Amorim makes clumsy 9/11 analogy on 25th anniversary of terror attack - before taking fresh swipe at Old Trafford legends in bizarre press conference
Sports.content:
Ruben Amorim was forced to correct himself after making an awkward comparison involving an aeroplane accident while explaining how his team learns from setbacks during a press conference on the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks.

The 41-year-old former Manchester United head coach, who was appointed AC Milan manager in June, was discussing the process of implementing his philosophy with his new side when he turned to the analogy.

He said: 'I think we should improve in every training session. I expect that my players understand, it's like when you have an accident with an airplane, you learn something from.'

Amorim then quickly added: 'It's not a good comparison, you understand what I mean.

'If something wrong happens, we take a lot of information and we put it in training sessions.'

Amorim has courted controversy with his comments in the past, including when he called his United side the 'worst team in the history of Manchester United' after a Premier League defeat to Brighton last January, a remark for which he later apologised.

The 41-year-old former Manchester United head coach was discussing the process of implementing his philosophy with his new side when he turned to the analogy

'I'm a young guy and sometimes I make a mistake,' he said at the time. 'And that's why I don't (usually) talk after the game. This game, I needed to talk and maybe it was a mistake and then I get more nervous and go to the (news) conference really nervous and say things I shouldn't say, that's it. Sometimes I'm a young guy and I make mistakes.'

The Portuguese manager presided over United's lowest-ever Premier League finish (15th), and won just 38.1 per cent of his games in charge in all competitions, the worst rate of any United manager in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era.

His time in charge saw a constant back-and-forth with former players, including Gary Neville, Roy Keane and Paul Scholes. As United's results deteriorated, the pundits regularly criticised his tactics, while he was repeatedly drawn into the debate.

Amorim's move to Milan appears to have brought a familiar challenge, with many of the club's former greats holding influential roles in the media.

Discussing the influence of club legends in the media, Amorim said on Friday: 'I was in a club in the past with a lot of legends, and they have big opinions, and they talk a lot about things. They lived in a time that was completely different.'

Sports.title: Thug who 'hit, bound and threatened' Man City star Gianluigi Donnarumma and his pregnant girlfriend with a knife during Paris flat raid sentenced to nine years in prison
Sports.content:
Thug who 'hit, bound and threatened' Man City star Gianluigi Donnarumma and his pregnant girlfriend with a knife during Paris flat raid sentenced to nine years in prison

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A 21-year-old has been sentenced to nine years in prison for his role in a terrifying break-in of Gianluigi Donnarumma and his then-pregnant girlfriend's flat in Paris three years ago.

The Man City goalkeeper and Alessia Elefante, whom he has since married and had a child with, were hit, bound and threatened with a knife after robbers broke into their flat.

The incident took place in Avenue Montaigne, one of Paris' most famous and luxurious streets, with Donnarumma and his partner asleep at the time.

A Paris criminal court has sentenced Ilyas Kherbouch, 21, to nine years in prison plus an €80,000 fine for his role in the shocking attack, Marca reports.

Kherbouch, who is nicknamed 'Ganito' and caused numerous disruptions to the two-day trial, saw his co-defendent Khyan Mamouni, 22, acquitted, while Moktar Diop, 24, was sentenced to five years in prison - two of which were suspended.

Donnarumma did not give evidence but a witness statement from him shed further light on what went on.

Court documents revealed how Donnarumma was woken by a man saying 'shh', before he was hit in the face with a knuckle duster and threatened with a knife.

Gianluigi Donnarumma and his then-pregnant girlfriend Alessia Elefante were hit, bound and threatened with a knife by robbers in their Paris flat in 2023 (pictured together in 2024)

The thieves left with keys to supercars, cash, watches and luxury handbags after robbing Donnarumma and Elefante (pictured in 2024)

The man then said: 'The watches, the watches'.

As per court documents, Donnarumma replied: 'I showed him the one on the dressing table, an Audemars Piguet.' Those watches can have a value worth up to hundreds of thousands of euros.

His partner told investigators that she was also woken up by the thieves who attacked her and shouted: 'The money, the watches.'

She subsequently gave them a Cartier watch, jewellery and €2,000 (£1718) in cash.

Elefante was then accosted for the code to a safe. However, she revealed she didn't know it and said it was empty anyway.

'They got angry thinking that I was lying,' she told investigators. 'They pulled me by the hair and one of them hit me on the thighs. I said I was pregnant but they continued.'

Donnarumma did then give them the code to the safe, but as Elefante had warned, there was nothing in there.

The court was told that the robbers left with keys to a Mercedes and a Lamborghini, cash, watches and luxury handbags.

Police also added that the four robbers managed to get into the flat by using a ladder to climb onto the roof, before they lowered themselves onto the balcony and broke in through windows.

Two individuals that are already in prison - Ilyas Kherbouch, a 21-year-old with at least 11 criminal convictions, and Khyan Mamouni - are accused of masterminding and ordering the robbery from their cells. They both deny the charges.

Kherbouch, who escaped from jail in March and spent 13 days on the run, caused a stir at the opening of the trial.

This came when he insulted and threatened police officers when they told his brother to leave the court.

'Come here, you,' he told them. 'What are you going to do?'

When warned that he could be expelled from the courtroom, he replied: 'I couldn’t care less. I don’t want to be present at the trial. I don’t give a s***.'

Donnarumma, now 27 and at Man City, was playing for PSG at the time of the terrifying ordeal

Two of the robbers, who were under the age of 18 when the incident happened, have already been given jail sentences of three and four years respectively at a children's court.

Another defendant Moktar Diop, 24, admitted to taking part but is not accused of resorting to violence, while a fourth suspect died by suicide in 2024. He had previously admitted to being involved but told investigators he had come under pressure from his accomplices.

Donnarumma and his partner's lawyers said previously that they were 'still profoundly shocked'.

Sports.title: Richarlison's move to Brazil COLLAPSES: Spurs star fails to agree terms with Vasco da Gama as Roberto De Zerbi issues cryptic response to threat of legal action amid contract row
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi insists there are no regrets at Tottenham about the handling of Richarlison's future - with the forward rejecting the chance to move to Vasco da Gama in Brazil, according to reports in the country.

The Brazilian was left out of De Zerbi's squad after rejecting a move to Everton before the transfer deadline, which caused a move for Iliman Ndiaye to fall through.

One of his final hopes of getting out of the north London club was a move to his homeland, but it is reported that there is no agreement on personal terms, despite expectations from Vasco that Tottenham would be open to a deal.

It is understood a three-and-a-half-year deal was on offer for the 29-year-old, but that he is not currently looking to move back to Brazil.

After the Ndiaye deal fell through, Spurs turned instead to sign Mykhailo Mudryk who was injured in training this week and out for up to two months.

'I am sorry because I have one player less on the list,' said De Zerbi. 'Richarlison is a good guy. I spoke with him a lot and spent time trying to convince him to stay.

Roberto De Zerbi (left) has responded to Richarlison's (centre) threat of legal action against Tottenham

'But I know the truth. I know what happened in the last month, the last 45 days and I know the behaviour of Richarlison. And it's clear.

'I can't explain it because it's not right but I'm sorry because it could have been different and in a different way it could have been better.'

Richarlison, top scorer last season for Spurs with 11 Premier League goals, has been exploring legal action to have the final nine months of his contract nullified amid interest from Brazil.

Spurs have not scored in their first three games of the season and did not have a shot on target in the goalless draw at Nottingham Forest last week.

De Zerbi is certain there are enough goals in his team however and challenged Omar Marmoush to shoulder more of the burden.

'Marmoush is playing well,' said the Spurs boss. 'In Nottingham he played a good game, not a fantastic game, not fantastic with the last decision. But he was alive and in the game. He seemed to be dangerous.

'He is smart, understands football. In terms of goals, he is not Harry Kane but he can score more goals than he has done in the last two seasons.

'About Manchester City, I don't want to speak because not my experience but at Eintracht Frankfurt he scored lots of goals. If you analyse his qualities he can score more goals and has to demand more goals of himself.'

De Zerbi could look to pair Marmoush with Dominic Solanke in the search for the right chemistry in attack. 'They can play together,' he said. 'When we signed Marmoush we thought he could play with another striker or alone.'

Sports.title: Why Enceladus is the one to beat and the 18-1 outsider that catches the eye: Your ultimate guide to Doncaster's St Leger
Sports.content:
Why Enceladus is the one to beat and the 18-1 outsider that catches the eye: Your ultimate guide to Doncaster's St Leger

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The final British Classic of the Flat season is here - the St Leger at Doncaster.

Daily Mail Sport's expert Sam Turner runs through the 11 runners vying for glory and the £390,000 prize pot in the 3.35pm feature race on Saturday afternoon...

ACTION

Creditable runner-up to Item in York’s Dante Stakes back in the spring, but has regressed in four starts since, admittedly all at Group One level. Hard to imagine him bouncing back to form here, even over a new trip.

Sam Turner's star rating: ★

ALDERMAN

Ran a fine race in the Derby when a huge price, but disappointed on latest start at Newmarket when upped in trip. This new distance represents a step into the unknown.

Sam Turner's star rating: ★

CHRISTMAS DAY

Winner of the Derby in testing conditions before running commendably in the Irish version which placed less emphasis on stamina. A shade below-par in a strong renewal of the Great Voltigeur last time and could easily bounce back upped in trip.

Sam Turner's star rating: ★ ★ ★ ★

ENCELADUS

Progressive Royal Ascot winner who confirmed he would be a force at Group level with a smooth victory in the Gordon Stakes at Goodwood. A sizeable unit with gears, he may find further improvement over this new trip with the cheekpieces applied for the first time.

Sam Turner's star rating: ★ ★ ★ ★ ★

Enceladus is a progressive Royal Ascot winner who reinforced his status at Glorious Goodwood

GALIYAN

Looked a horse going places courtesy of a maiden win at Chester in the spring, but his career has stalled somewhat since, including when too keen for his own good at York in the Voltigeur last time out. Others preferred.

Sam Turner's star rating: ★

GOLDEN STORY

Juvenile maiden win at this venue reads well given he beat the now 106-rated Infraad with comfort and is less exposed than most. Capable of better going forward but can race exuberantly and would need to settle better to see out this trip.

ST LEGER BETTING ODDS Enceladus - 2/1 Christmas Day - 9/4 Pierre Bonnard - 3/1 Highwayman - 12/1 Hatteen - 18/1 Alderman - 28/1 Amelia Earhart - 28/1 Galiyan - 33/1 Action - 50/1 Golden Story - 50/1 Rebel Rocker - 70/1 *Odds courtesy of Paddy Power

Sam Turner's star rating: ★

HATTEEN

Has progressed with each run this summer and posted a sizeable career best in handicap company at Goodwood on his latest start. Has already proved his effectiveness at this venue and will appreciate any cut in the ground. Live chance at a double-figure price.

Sam Turner's star rating: ★ ★ ★ ★

HIGHWAYMAN

Most of his early days were spent as a hold-up performer, however a mid-season switch to staying trips and more aggressive rides have unmasked excellent results. More required at this level, but he is with the right trainer to achieve just that.

Sam Turner's star rating: ★ ★ ★ ★

PIERRE BONNARD

Has appeared a likely type for this assignment for a while, with this more demanding test of stamina sure to suit. Reversed placings with his old rival and stablemate Christmas Day at York, so there is unlikely to be much between the pair here again.

Sam Turner's star rating: ★ ★ ★ ★

REBEL ROCKER

Likeable colt who outran his odds in the Derby to take sixth at a sizeable price. Entitled to be sharper for his first run since then when fourth in the Geoffrey Freer at Newbury but did not hit the line strongly there and there is a strong suspicion he will be outstayed here.

Sam Turner's star rating: ★

AMELIA EARHEART

Quirky filly who was well beaten in the British and Irish Oaks prior to disappointing in the Lillie Langtry Stakes. Back to form in a Cork Group Three, but difficult to see her being able to challenge at this level.

Sam Turner's star rating: ★

Sam Turner's verdict: Christmas Day and Pierre Bonnard already have solid Group One form and, although it was disappointing the duo were beaten in the Great Voltigeur at York, their conqueror (Maltese Cross) is second favourite for the Arc next month. Goodwood winner ENCELADUS must improve again to reach their level but has the scope to do just that and can give trainer Joseph O’Brien his second win in the race following Galileo Chrome’s success in 2020. Hatteen is a likeable stayer and can emerge best of the bigger-priced contenders.

SAM'S TOP TIPS FOR DAY THREE Doncaster, 4.15pm – Moonfall / Inspired Moonfall and Inspired are two in-form, progressive handicappers who look worth supporting in this highly competitive handicap. The former was picked off close home by Ascot specialist Hickory last week, but ought to be on the scene again with this assignment likely to suit a strong traveller, while Inspired again advertised his well-being at York last Sunday and could be on the scene once more under a penalty. Leopardstown, 5.00pm – Almaqam (eachway) The prospect of rain at Leopardstown would be music to the ears of Almaqam’s trainer Ed Walker who was distraught when his stable star was collared on the line in the Juddmonte International at York last month. Bookmakers have again appeared to dismiss his chance this week, but if all eight runners go to post he makes plenty of each-way appeal given he has already won a Group 1 in Ireland this summer so clearly enjoys travelling. Doncaster, 5.20pm – Sportingsilvermine (eachway) Given this is his 11th start of the season, no one could accuse Sportingsilvermine of being either lazy or unexposed, but he was a creditable third in last year’s running of this race and double figure quotes about his chance look more than fair. Marco Ghiani, currently enjoying his best season, is again in the saddle and the selection found easy ground over a mile and a half at York beyond him last time so, if the rain avoids Town Moor, he could go well again back at ten furlongs.

Meanwhile in Ireland, trainer Ed Walker is happy to see Alamqam fly ‘under the radar’ as he plots the demise of old rivals Constitution River and Item in Saturday's Royal Bahrain Irish Champion Stakes.

The enthralling Group 1 Leopardstown showpiece has drawn together the first three home from last month’s Juddmonte International, along with sixth-placed Hawk Mountain, with Almaqam looking to reverse placings with winner Item.

Constitution River, winner of the French Derby and Coral-Eclipse, was beaten three and a half lengths on the Knavesmire yet is favourite to turn the tables on the two English raiders, a scenario which surprised Walker.

‘I was quite interested when I saw the headline about the Juddmonte rematch in the Racing Post this week and Alamqam didn’t get a mention which made me chuckle,’ he said.

‘He’s actually been fresh and well (since York) and has been in great form - he’s come out of the race very well.

‘Realistically, he’s probably got two more targets left this year in the Irish and English Champion Stakes and he is really well suited with a little bit of ease in the ground.

‘He’s just had two very frustrating dry summers which has made life very difficult for us.

‘He is very good on his day and if he goes under the radar, then that’s fine by us.’

Sports.title: Fans hail 'beautiful' national anthem as US Open honors 9/11 anniversary ahead of all-American semifinal between Ben Shelton and Frances Tiafoe
Sports.content:
The US Open marked the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks with a touching moment of silence and a stirring rendition of the national anthem before Ben Shelton squared off with fellow American Frances Tiafoe in the semifinals.

In a performance described as a 'moving tribute' by The Athletic's Lukas Weese and 'beautiful' by many others in attendance, pop singer Jojo belted out The Star-Spangled Banner accompanied by the New York Vocal Collective choir. Meanwhile, Mervin Primeaux-O-Bryant performed in Sign Language as Army cadets from West Point unfurled a large American flag on the court.

'JoJo with an absolutely gorgeous national anthem to commemorate 9/11,' one admirer wrote on X, adding: '10s across.'

'JoJo needs to sing eveeeery National anthem for the US at sporting events!!' another added. 'She can saaaaang baby!!!'

Even those who are admittedly down on the anthem appreciated JoJo's performance.

'I still feel like the National Anthem has zero meaning in the current state of the country but gotdamn Jojo just ATE that,' one fan joked.

JoJo sings the national anthem during a ceremony marking the 25th anniversary of 9/11

Mervin Primeaux-O-Bryant performed in Sign Language as Army cadets from West Point unfurled a large American flag on the court before

In a performance described as a 'moving tribute' by The Athletic's Lukas Weese, pop singer Jojo belted out The Star-Spangled Banner accompanied by the New York Vocal Collective

Another fan claimed JoJo 'bodied the national anthem,' which appeared to be meant as a compliment.

But many others were far more serious in their adulation.

'Well that #USOpen National Anthem, on the 25th Anniversary of Sept 11, in New York City, in a match between 2 Americans…. brought all the emotion,' one fan wrote. 'Incredible.'

Born Joanna Noëlle Levesque in Brattleboro, Vermont, the 35-year-old JoJo does have some practice with the tune after performing it at WWE matches and a New England Patriots game in Foxborough, Massachusetts, where she was raised.

A total of 2,753 people died at New York's World Trade Center when a pair of hijacked airplanes crashed into the Twin Towers. That death toll includes 343 firefighters and 71 law-enforcement officers.

JoJo's performance fittingly took place before an All-American semifinal, which means an American man will be in the singles final for the first time since 2024. No American man has won a US Open singles title since Andy Roddick in 2003.

Sports.title: Ben Shelton reaches first-ever Grand Slam final at US Open as he outduels good friend Frances Tiafoe in all-American showdown... with a chance to finally end 23-year US drought
Sports.content:
Ben Shelton will look to become the first American man to win a Grand Slam in 23 years after beating his close friend Frances Tiafoe 4-6, 6-3, 6-3, 7-5 to book his place in the US Open final.

It was a heart-wrenching moment for Tiafoe, who played and lost his third semi-final inside Arthur Ashe Stadium, and misses the chance to become the first Black player to feature in a US Open men’s final since the legend who gave the court its name. Instead, that honour will go to Shelton, after another towering performance on the heels of knocking out defending champion Carlos Alcaraz.

Tiafoe exited the stadium with a towel draped over his head to hide the waves of emotion. On the court, Shelton paid tribute to his ‘big brother’.

‘To be honest, every time we get to take this court together and play each other is super special,’ Shelton said. ‘To be able to light it up in front of you guys is the best feeling that there is.'

Shelton has not played at this stage in New York since 2023. ’I think I’ve grown up, I’m more mature, more focused,’ he said. ‘I know what my job is and I’m hundred percent committed.’

Now, he will play French Open champion Alexander Zverev. It is Shelton’s Grand Slam final debut, and Zverev’s sixth.

Ben Shelton will play his first Grand Slam final on Sunday after defeating Frances Tiafoe in his US Open semi-final

The 28-year-old has played and lost three semi-finals in New York and had taken the first set

’I’m going to need you guys on Sunday to bring the energy,’ he asked of the crowd. ‘I’m going for it here. I’m going to leave it all on the court. Let’s do this for the USA.’

Moved from the afternoon men’s semi-final slot to 7pm primetime, Tiafoe and Shelton delivered on their promise of a show, and more, playing four break-neck sets where there was little to separate their quality and nerve.

But as he showed against Alcaraz, Shelton has the weapons needed to wrench momentum with a clinical edge, and he took no more time than was necessary to down his countryman.

He did so as the slight underdog. Tiafoe has made the US Open his home, the crowd in his thrall as he regularly serves up big performance after big performance regardless of the form of his season. He thrives in the night sessions in particular, capable of hitting new levels under the lights.

Locked in amid a strong run of form in 2026, Tiafoe has rewarded them more than ever on this run, and despite loyalties being broadly divided between the two Americans, he remained the favourite by an edge.

He surfed on this wave through the first set, playing immaculate tennis while Shelton looked restless and struggled to settle. Tiafoe had his full bag of tricks on display, including a smart net game, while Shelton’s variety failed him in the early stages - with his drop shots undercooked, and forehands at times overeager.

What remained on song was his serve, that 140mph weapon that can be so fast as to be invisible. While Shelton was reeling off aces, Tiafoe was frequently sending down second serves. But the 28-year-old’s game stayed neat, with just three unforced errors played, while Shelton went up and down, peppering in double faults, the second of which earned Tiafoe the crucial break.

But if beating Alcaraz has taught Shelton anything, it’s patience. There is a confidence to his game that, in the wake of that momentous win, makes a comeback feel like nothing more than a waiting game.

Determined to speed things up, Shelton was in attack mode as he roared into the second set with a straightforward hold of his serve before a rapid break of Tiafoe’s.

Anything you can do, Tiafoe seemed to say, as he sent down a forehand which kissed the line and set up his first break point to love. He didn’t pull it off then, but the second attempt a point later was good.

Big Foe 💔💔💔💔💔💔💔💔💔💔 pic.twitter.com/SIGoHbJPOV — The Tennis Letter (@TheTennisLetter) September 12, 2026

Shelton and Tiafoe are close friends and embraced at the net, despite the older man's visible pain at losing again

The 23-year-old's girlfriend, soccer star Trinity Rodman, watched nervously from the stands

Among the notable faces in the stands were Knicks hero Jalen Brunson and actor Ben Stiller

The young American said that he has learned focus and commitment to his game since playing his last New York semi-final in 2023

Tiafoe is a dogged and creative returner and for much of the match there was little to separate the two stars

Shelton was swept up by his team, including his father and coach - and ex-pro - Bryan Shelton

Level on serve, Shelton gave the crowd their first big cry of amazement as the rallies grew longer, surviving 16 impossible shots until Tiafoe made the forehand error. With his blood up, Shelton bashed back a down-the-line winner for break point, and took it, snatching momentum back towards him and swiping the set.

The tennis, already miraculous, only improved into the third set. Seeing their champion fading, the crowd screamed their support for Tiafoe as he paused to serve, down set point. But as the players reset to deuce for the seventh, the older man could only hold off the onslaught for so long.

Tiafoe often came off the better in the longer exchanges but they took their toll as the third set wore on, and Shelton hoovered up shorter points. He looked visibly fatigued, and only marginally fresher stepping out for the fourth after the set break.

His mood was no better when chair umpire Aurelie Tourte failed to tell Shelton that Tiafoe wasn’t ready to receive at break point, advantage.

Tiafoe had held up his hands and said ‘sorry, sorry’, but when Tourte failed to speak up and Shelton sent down the serve, both players rounded on her.

‘Why didn’t you say something?’ Tiafoe queried, while Shelton snapped: ‘You’ve got to say something immediately!’

The point was replayed, but Tiafoe never got his chance back. Shelton had his game face on as he put away his second advantage with a smacked forehand straight towards Tiafoe. There was no apology that followed it, only a glare thrown in Tiafoe’s direction.

But Tiafoe didn’t take a step back and looked the more comfortable player in the early stages of the fourth as his first serve firmed up. As Shelton struck his 19th ace to make it 5-4 on serve, there were no problems there either.

The pressure was on Tiafoe, however, to serve and stay in the match, with the hope of winning that longed-for spot in his home Grand Slam final.

Despite Shelton climbing into the match at 40-30, it did not tell, with Tiafoe nerveless at the net to strike a forehand winner. It preceded an enormous yell from the Maryland-native.

But it was only a stay of execution. The next time he stepped up to serve, the crowd again screaming for him to keep fighting on, Tiafoe tightened up, and had to stare down three match point chances. Shelton only needed two, as Tiafoe sent down the fatal double fault.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
