China Southern Airlines will restart regular passenger flights between Guangzhou and New Delhi from September 21, the Global Times reported on Saturday.The announcement came ahead of Chinese president Xi Jinpingâs visit to India for the Brics summit. The airline said the resumption would take its total operations across eight round-trip routes in South Asia to more than 100 flights a week. The Guangzhou-New Delhi service had been suspended for six years.Air connectivity between India and China has gradually improved in recent months.Air China resumed its Beijing-Delhi service in April, while China Eastern Airlines restarted direct flights between Kunming and Kolkata on April 18.Indian carrier IndiGo also launched a daily non-stop service between Kolkata and Shanghai on March 30. The airline had earlier restored flights from Kolkata to Guangzhou and later began operating from Delhi to the Chinese city.The resumption of direct flights followed confirmation from Indiaâs ministry of external affairs. Air links between the two countries had been suspended during the Covid-19 pandemic and amid tensions following the Doklam and Galwan standoffs.Xi left Beijing on Saturday for the 18th Brics summit in New Delhi at Modiâs invitation, Chinaâs state news agency Xinhua reported.The Chinese president is scheduled to hold a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi later in the day.Xiâs delegation includes Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China and director of its General Office, and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi.According to Xinhua, Xi is expected to advance proposals on cooperation among Global South countries, building on his remarks at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek.Brics has become a major platform for emerging economies to coordinate on trade, finance, technology, development and global governance. The grouping also seeks to promote greater cooperation among countries of the Global South.

World.title: SC's 13 queries to FSSAI: 'Give details on shape, size, colour of food label'
World.content:
Supreme Court Justice JB Pardiwala questioned why the FSSAI was taking a two-phased approach.

'Red hexagon' to send out warning to customers

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court has directed FSSAI to spell out details of how front-of-pack food warning labels will look, their shape, size, colour, placement on packets and the timeline of implementation, leaving nothing to the discretion of the food regulator.The court also wanted to know how Centre plans to warn children about the dangers of junk food.After FSSAI agreed to implement labelling after being pushed by SC and filed an affidavit, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran put 13 questions to the regulator and gave 10 days' time for answers.Though SC acknowledged "significant progress" has been made by FSSAI on this issue of national importance, it said the regulator's affidavit was silent on various issues and several aspects of practical implementation required clarification.The 13 questions are part of the detailed order uploaded by the court on Friday, which also includes its observations from the previous day on why FSSAI proposed a two-phase rollout of the labelling requirements instead of implementing them in one go.According to FSSAIâs proposal, during Phase I, a red hexagonal warning would be placed on products high in two or more nutrients of concern, namely added fat, added sugar and salt, based on thresholds in the Dietary Guidelines for Indians, 2024.The warning could carry declarations such as âHIGH FATâ, âHIGH SUGARâ, âHIGH SALTâ and âHIGHLY SWEETENED BEVERAGEâ. The proposed Phase II would extend the warning to products high in any one of the specified nutrients. The order questions the regulator on what basis it suggested the inclusion of food products high in âtwo or moreâ nutrients of concern and certain sweetened beverages in Phase I, and the inclusion of food products high in âany oneâ nutrient of concern in Phase II, respectively.The court also said sugar, salt and fat are called the âUnholy Trinityâ and that âthe âunholinessâ arises not only from the added sugar and added fat in a food product but the total value of these nutrients available in a product, which has to be considered.â The Supreme Court incorporated the suggestion of advocate Rajiv Shankar Dvivedi that the threshold must be decided based on âtotal sugarâ and âtotal fatâ and not on the basis of âadded sugarâ and âadded fatâ. Referring to the 2021 FSSAI meeting, the Bench said, âIt is clear from the aforesaid minutes that âtotal sugarâ and âsaturated fatâ would be used for the purpose of the labelling. In this regard, we would like FSSAI to weigh in and indicate whether there has been a change in stance in comparison to the consensus arrived at in the aforesaid stakeholder consultation. If so, we would like to know how the underlying concerns are sought to be addressed.âThe court also asked the regulator: âWhat are the dimensions of the âred hexagonâ proposed to be used in the FoPL (labelling)? Whether it would have standardised specifications or whether it would be calculated in proportion to the area of the package? Whether the font size used for FoPL would be relative to the dimensions of the hexagon themselves? The manner and method of the placement of such hexagon(s)?â It further asked, âWhy has FSSAI suggested a combined/composite/singular hexagon for two or more nutrients of concern instead of separate/distinct/individual hexagons for each nutrient of concern?â The court posted the matter for hearing on September 28.

World.title: Employee of The American College in Madurai arrested in job scam, three others booked
World.content:
A 40-year-old employee of The American College in Madurai was arrested by the Madurai City Police in connection with a job scam concerning the college on Thursday (September 10, 2026).

The employee has been identified as V. Kalaiselvi. Based on a complaint lodged by a person named M. Soman of Karaikudi, the Central Crime Branch police also booked Kalaiselvi’s husband Vijayakumar, a temporary employee of the college; Daniel, a guest lecturer; and M. Dhavanmani Christober, a retired principal, on charges of cheating.

The police said that the four accused had cheated Soman of ₹15.75 lakh on the promise of getting his daughter a lecturer’s job in the English Department in 2024.

According to Soman, he had approached Daniel upon seeing an  about the recruitment of an Assistant Professor in the college. Daniel had introduced Soman and his family to Kalaiselvi and Vijayakumar, claiming that they were close relatives of the former principal.

The accused had sought ₹45 lakh for the post. Soman had given them ₹15.75 lakh in multiple instalments.

However, the accused neither got his daughter the promised job nor returned the money.

This is the second case registered by the Madurai City Police with regard to a job scam concerning the college. Previously, the Anna Nagar police had registered a similar case against a few persons, including the former principal.

World.title: Philippines begins identifying victims from ferry fire as dozens still missing
World.content:
Philippine authorities began the painstaking process of ‌identifying victims from a ferry fire on Saturday (September 12, 2026), a day after ​responders recovered bodies from the burned-out vessel, raising the death ⁠toll to at least 35 and leaving more than 50 people missing.

The bodies were transported to a port in Coron town, where temporary tents were set up for forensic teams ‌to process and identify the victims.

Near the port, some family members anxiously watched as responders in protective suits carried black body bags ‌from a Coast Guard vessel to temporary tents.

One of them was Anelyn ‌Magbanua, ⁠37, whose husband was returning to Coron after visiting their children ⁠in Manila when the ferry, which was carrying more than 130 people, caught fire near the end of its more than 20-hour journey.

"I hope he is not among the dead being brought ​off the ship. I hope he ‌is alive and has only drifted to another island," she said.

"It will be very difficult to accept if he's really gone," she said. "He loved his children very much."

Firefighters entered the ferry for the first time on Friday (September 11) after ‌extinguishing the blaze more than a day after it broke out, giving ​authorities access to areas that had been hard to reach because of thick smoke and extreme heat. The Coast Guard said burnt ⁠remains were discovered in the ferry's economy accommodation section.

Images released by the Coast Guard showed the scale of the destruction inside the vessel, with rows of steel ‌bed frames twisted by intense heat and blanketed in ash. Some photographs appeared to show skeletal remains among the debris.

Philippine Coast Guard official Geronimo Tuvilla said at a press conference on Saturday (September 12) that the immediate priority was to identify the victims and determine the cause of the fire.

A statement from the Maritime Industry Authority, citing survivor accounts, said two explosions were heard inside the vessel shortly ‌before the fire broke out.

One survivor interviewed by GMA News recalled seeing a small amount of ​smoke that turned into a fire and quickly spread through the ferry within seconds.

Questions also remained over the fate of the ⁠vessel's captain. Coast Guard spokesperson Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said at the same press conference that ⁠she had received information that he was alive, but added that the captain's name was not on the list of 43 confirmed survivors.

The ‌fire is the latest in a string of deadly maritime accidents in the Philippines, an archipelago of more than 7,600 islands where millions rely on ​ferries and small boats to travel between provinces and islands.

World.title: BRICS joint statement agreed upon, to be issued shortly
World.content:
Indian negotiators have managed to reach a consensus, sources confirmed to The Hindu, indicating that differences between Iran, UAE and Saudi Arabia over the wording of paragraph relating to the ongoing war have been resolved.

Keep track | BRICS Summit 2026 LIVE updates: PM Modi proposes 10-point proposal for global governanceK

Officials said that the BRICS countries had reached an understanding “on all aspects” over a joint statement to be released shortly. This is the first time the BRICS grouping founded by Russia, China, India, Brazil and South Africa that now includes UAE and Iran, as well as Saudi Arabia, is meeting after the US-Israel strikes on Iran and the assassination of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ali Khameini in February this year.

Iran’s retaliation against its Gulf neighbours, including the UAE and Saudi Arabia had set up discordant notes at all BRICS meetings in the run-up to the Summit being held in Delhi this weekend.

The negotiations were completed on Saturday (September 12, 2026) afternoon, with India’s negotiating team led by Secretary (Economic Relations) Sudhakar Dalela and officials from the Ministry of External Affairs.

However, the government has been engaging all levels with the 11-member BRICS leadership to try and forge the joint statement. On Friday (September 11), Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s meetings with Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian, and on Saturday (September 12) with Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Khalid bin Mohamad bin Zayed Al Nahyan are understood to have pushed the two sides together.

World.title: Social media opening doors to child marriages?
World.content:
Last year, the District Child Welfare Committee in Chennai dealt with a case where a 15-year-old girl from Nepal had married a 28-year-old man working in Chennai, the two having met on Instagram. With the help of friends, they got married in Chennai.

A month into the marriage, the girl was traced after she made a call to her sister in Nepal. The girl’s family lodged a complaint with the police following which India Child Protection, a civil society organisation working in the area of child protection, intervened to rescue the girl.

Social media and online dating are increasingly exposing vulnerable girls to greater risk of child marriage.

“With advancement in digital communication, the modus operandi in child marriage is changing, making more children vulnerable,” says Bhuwan Ribhu, a child rights activist and founder of Just Rights for Children.

Bhuwan Ribhu says trafficking is a borderless crime, and it requires a borderless response. Online methods of enticement or grooming for marriage, sexual abuse and trafficking have become possible irrespective of distance and geography.

In a study taken by NGO Save the Children, they observed that girls in India faced greater online risk of child marriage and trafficking during the pandemic. The agency continues to work with children and teachers to raise awareness about staying safe online.

According to the National Family Health Survey (2019-21), the national average in India for child marriage is 23%. The prevalence rate in India for child marriage has fallen by 10 per cent. The Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat campaign launched by the Central Government in November 2024 promises to make India child marriage-free by 2030 and is seeing various state governments running different initiatives.

A dedicated CMPO needed

Natharsha Malim H, state coordinator - Tamil Nadu, India Child Protection, says while Tamil Nadu has been making steady progress in reporting and stopping child marriages, gaps continue to exist.

Tamil Nadu, he says, does not have Child Marriage Prohibition Officers (CMPOs) that are appointed to prevent marriages, gather evidence, raise awareness and report data. The District Social Welfare Officer (DSWO) is notified as the Child Marriage Prohibition Officer of the concerned district.

“This is an additional role that the DSWO takes up. We have been asking for a dedicated person to be appointed as many other states have done based on a Supreme Court recommendation,” says Malim.

For example, in Karnataka, the Department of Women and Child Welfare has included pre-university (PU) college principals as child marriage prohibition officers, whose responsibility is to prevent any girl child studying in their college from marrying before 18 years.

Dedicated officials tasked with curbing this practice is particularly required in places such as Salem, Dindigul, Namakal and Cuddalore which has reported maximum cases of child marriages, says Malim. Grama panchayats have to be empowered in these districts to curb child marriage

A rule book for intervention

Malim notes that State Governments have to draw up a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for elimination of child marriages.

“The Supreme Court came out with a landmark judgement on child marriages in October 2024, but Tamil Nadu is yet to come out with an SOP,” he says.

Panchayats that make an earnest effort to stop child marriage should be rewarded; and the bravery of young girls that resist coercion by family into child marriage should also be acknowledged.

Bhuwan Ribhu cites the example of a study done by India Child Protection in 2025, wherein cases in Assam dropped by 84 percent following a continuous crackdown by law-enforcement authorities.

How to report a child marriage File a complaint with * Child Marriage Prohibition Officer * District Magistrate * Nearest police station * District Child Protection Unit * ASHA Unit of District Legal Services Authority * Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat portal https://stopchildmarriage.wcd.gov.in Source: Ministry of Women and Child Development

Although Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 has been in existence for decades, enforcement leaves a lot to be desired.

“With amendments to the law and judgments by the Supreme Court, we have been able to see much impact on the ground, along with greater awareness,” says Ribhu, adding, “awareness needs to be supplemented with the enforcement of policies, accountability of institutions, and the use of technology for monitoring.”

Residents association in Chennai hails UN declaration

On September 4, 2026, when the United Nations General Assembly declared November 27 as the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage, a residents group in Anna Nagar celebrated the announcement.

A small number of residents, close to 150, of Kambar Colony in Anna Nagar gathered at the park in the neighbourhood to watch the live proceedings of the United Nations General Assembly on the designation of November 27 as the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage.

The programme was organised by the ICWO Tamil Nadu and Kambar Colony Welfare Association. The designation is a significant global commitment to strengthening awareness, prevention and action against child, early and forced marriage. This is a victory for children and civil society organisation that have been fighting to end child marriage.

Awareness banners and charts were displayed, and the gathering concluded with an oath-taking ceremony to strengthen the community’s commitment to end child marriage.

ICWO is a partner agency with Just Rights with Children in Chennai, working with educational institutions and communities on rights concerning children.

A.J. Hariharan, founder secretary, ICWO, says reporting is the key to preventing child marriage. He notes: “we work closely with schools and colleges to help eradicate child marriage. All what we ask them is report any cases of child marriage to the helpline number or a teacher.”

ChildLine Helpline 1098 can also be dialled to report a case.
