World.title: Iranian president forecasts development of BRICS countries via stronger economic ties
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 12. The strengthening of financial and economic relations among BRICS member countries can lead to their development.

According to the information portal of the Iranian Presidential Administration, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian made the remarks during a meeting with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in India on September 12.

"Developing economic ties among BRICS member countries is of great importance. All member states can take steps to foster these relations," he noted.

Pezeshkian stated that large-scale attacks had been launched against Iran in recent months. Although opposing parties attempted to sow discord between the Iranian state and its citizens, these attacks served to further unite the Iranian people, who stood firm against them with all their might.

"The U.S. and Israel will not achieve their objectives in Iran, thanks to the unity of the Iranian people. Iran has strengthened its ties with neighboring and Muslim nations. Iran has long-standing relations with its neighbors, and these ties will continue to expand day by day," he pointed out.

Pezeshkian said that Iran and Ethiopia have enjoyed friendly relations for over 70 years. The two countries have always stood by each other, and undoubtedly, their relations will be further strengthened.

During the meeting, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali also noted the existence of numerous economic and cultural ties between Ethiopia and Iran's neighbors, expressing interest in developing similar relations with Iran.

World.title: 31st Baku Rhythmic Gymnastics Championship concludes second competition day (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 12. The second competition day of the 31st Baku Rhythmic Gymnastics Championship has concluded.

The Azerbaijan Gymnastics Federation (AGF) reported this.

On the second day of the competition, gymnasts in the pre-junior, junior and youth age categories demonstrated their skills. In addition to individual programs, group exercises were also performed throughout the day.

In the all-around competition among pre-juniors born in 2018, Humay Asgarzade won the gold medal, Nasrin Bashirli took silver, and Amina Bakirova won bronze.

Among pre-juniors born in 2017, Miray Salamzade took first place, Miray Hasanaliyeva finished second, and Asya Mahmuzade placed third.

In the competition among gymnasts born in 2016, Nazli Mammadzade took the top spot on the podium. Zeynab Ismayilova won silver, while Aylin Gozalova took bronze.

In the all-around competition among juniors born in 2013, Amina Novruzova won the gold medal. Gulluzar Sharifova took silver, while Sara Atakishiyeva won bronze.

At the end of the competition day, group exercise teams also competed for medals. In the pre-junior category, the Ocaq 2 team took first place, Ocaq 3 finished second, and Ocaq 1 placed third. Among juniors, Ocaq 3 won gold, Ocaq 2 took silver, and Ocaq 4 won bronze.

Thus, the second competition day of the Baku Championship concluded with the winners determined in the individual and group programs.

World.title: Kyrgyzstan predicts further enhancement of cooperation with Azerbaijan - ambassador
World.content:
AGHDARA, Azerbaijan, September 12. Relations between Azerbaijan and Kyrgyzstan are taking on an increasingly strategic and close character, Kyrgyzstan’s Ambassador to Azerbaijan Maksat Mamytkanov made the remarks in an interview with Trend on the second day of the visit by representatives of the diplomatic corps accredited in Azerbaijan to Karabakh and East Zangazur.

The ambassador noted that significant agreements regarding the development of cooperation between the two countries were reached following the state visit of President of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev to Kyrgyzstan a month ago.

"First and foremost, an agreement on allied relations was signed between Azerbaijan and Kyrgyzstan. In accordance with this agreement, our relations have risen to the highest level of interaction between the two countries.

In line with these alliance agreements, our future cooperation will take on a broader scope. Therefore, we anticipate closer cooperation and greater activity across all areas of interstate relations," Mamytkanov added.

Representatives of the diplomatic corps accredited in Azerbaijan are visiting Karabakh and Eastern Zangazur accompanied by Hikmet Hajiyev, Assistant to the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan and Head of the Foreign Policy Affairs Department of the Presidential Administration.

The visit involves a 150-member delegation representing 58 countries and nine international organizations.

On September 11, the diplomatic representatives visited Khankendi and Shusha. In Khankendi, the delegation first toured the Khankendi Railway and Bus Terminal Complex, where construction work is underway. They then visited the Cultural Center in Khankendi. The diplomats also visited Victory Park and took a group photo in front of the Victory Arch. The visit also included a tour of Karabakh University.

In Shusha, the delegation inspected ongoing restoration and reconstruction work and visited the First Residential Quarter, the construction site of the New Shusha Mosque, the Molla Panah Vagif Museum-Mausoleum Complex, Jidir Duzu, Karabakh Street, Sadigjan’s House, the Ashaghi Govhar Agha Mosque, Shusha Central Square, the Shusha Creative Center and the Uzeyir Hajibeyli House Museum.

The diplomats also took a group photo in front of the Shusha Fortress walls and attended an official reception held to mark the Independence Day of the United Mexican States.

World.title: Hikmet Hajiyev visits Albanian churches with diplomatic corps representatives
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 12. Hikmet Hajiyev, Assistant to the President of Azerbaijan and head of the Foreign Policy Affairs Department of the Presidential Administration, visited the Gandzasar and Khudavang churches together with representatives of the diplomatic corps.

Hajiyev made the remarks in a post on his X account.

He said the Gandzasar and Khudavang churches are an integral part of the ancient Albanian Christian heritage.

“Gandzasar Church was built in the 13th century by Hasan Jalal Dawla, ruler of Caucasian Albania, and is one of the important pieces of evidence of the centuries-old Christian heritage of Caucasian Albania,” Hajiyev said.

The presidential aide emphasized that during the years of occupation, the monuments were subjected to external interventions carried out under the guise of temporary “restoration,” which damaged their architectural authenticity and original character.

“Every historical, cultural and religious monument in Azerbaijan, regardless of its origin or religious affiliation, is an integral part of our country’s rich cultural heritage. The Azerbaijani state remains committed to their preservation, protection and restoration,” he said.

Hajiyev noted that Azerbaijan’s experience in preserving its multicultural and multi-religious heritage has gained international recognition.

“We are ready to share this experience with other countries, including our neighbors,” the presidential aide emphasized.

He also called on media outlets spreading false reports and misleading narratives on the issue to visit the monuments and see the reality on the ground for themselves.

“Seeing is believing,” Hajiyev said.

Representatives of the diplomatic corps accredited in Azerbaijan are visiting Karabakh and East Zangazur under the guidance of Hikmet Hajiyev, Assistant to the President of Azerbaijan and head of the Foreign Policy Affairs Department of the Presidential Administration.

A delegation of 150 people representing 58 countries and nine international organizations is taking part in the visit.

On Sept. 11, representatives of the diplomatic corps visited Khankendi and Shusha. In Khankendi, the diplomats first toured the Khankendi Railway and Bus Station Complex, where construction work is underway. They then visited the Cultural Center in Khankendi. The delegation also visited the Victory Park and took a commemorative photo in front of the Victory Arch. As part of the visit, the diplomats also toured Karabakh University.

In Shusha, the delegation familiarized itself with restoration and reconstruction work underway in the city and visited the First Residential Complex, the construction site of the New Shusha Mosque, the Molla Panah Vagif Mausoleum-Museum Complex, Jidir Duzu, Karabakh Street, the Sadigjan House, the Lower Govhar Agha Mosque, Shusha Central Square, the Shusha Creative Center and the Uzeyir Hajibeyli House Museum.

The diplomats also took a commemorative photo in front of the Shusha Fortress walls and attended an official reception marking the Independence Day of the Republic of Mexico.

World.title: Wild pursuit and carjacking across Sydney's west leaves two children injured
World.content:
There have been scenes of mayhem across Sydney's west, with a carjacking, collision and stabbing after a motorist drove into oncoming traffic on a busy motorway with two children on board.

Police were called to carry out a welfare check on a 36-year-old driver in Belmore, but began a pursuit after he refused to pull over.

"When the driver allegedly failed to stop as directed, a police pursuit was initiated," NSW Police said in a statement.

"The pursuit continued into Auburn before it was terminated due to the manner of the man's driving."

Police said the man then drove on the wrong side of the M4 Motorway before hitting an oncoming vehicle.

Police say the pursuit was stopped at Auburn due to the "manner of the man's driving". (ABC News)

He then got out of the car with the two children and allegedly tried to steal a car.

A 25-year-old man intervened and during a scuffle suffered a stab wound to his hand.

The offender, police allege, then stole the vehicle of a woman who had stopped to help before bundling the two children into her car and speeding off westbound along the M4 Motorway.

He stopped on the Cumberland Highway at Wentworthville and was arrested by an off-duty police officer with help from bystanders.

He was taken to hospital under police guard.

The children suffered minor injuries and were taken to Westmead Children's Hospital as a precaution.

Police are still waiting to interview the man as they piece together what has happened.

World.title: Live: Lions stun Crows with outrageous early blitz in sudden-death semi
World.content:
(Getty Images)

Hello and welcome back to ABC Sport's live blog coverage of the 2026 AFL season. Only five teams and four games remain this year, the stakes rising with every kick of the ball and setting up a second crucial semifinal here tonight.

At the Gabba this evening the reigning premier Brisbane, champion of each of the last two seasons and a popular pick to make it a third in 2026, puts its streak on the line against an Adelaide side now filled with confidence and fearful of nobody.

The Lions are coming off a chastening defeat to Sydney in last week's qualifying final, the Crows a stirring elimination final win over the Bulldogs. The prize is a preliminary final date with Hawthorn next week.

It's a big evening for both clubs, so stick around and savour what we hope will be another classic final.

World.title: Hawks' AFLW win soured by skipper's sickening leg injury
World.content:
Aine McDonagh has fired Hawthorn to an 11-point win over the Western Bulldogs that was soured by captain Emily Bates's serious leg injury.

Bates was taken off the field on a stretcher at the Kennedy Community Centre today after her right leg twisted underneath her in a tackle late in the third quarter.

The decorated 30-year-old, who played her 100th AFLW match a week earlier, was expected to be taken to hospital for further assessment.

The Hawks also lost Laura Stone (concussion) after an early head clash with an opponent and were 11 points down at half-time.

But Daniel Webster's side piled on five unanswered goals in the third quarter — four of those before Bates's injury — to set up their 6.5 (41) to 4.6 (30) victory.

The result lifted Hawthorn (3-2 win-loss record) into the top eight, leapfrogging the Bulldogs (3-2) on percentage.

Irish key forward McDonagh kicked a career-best four majors, extending her lead at the top of this season's goal-kicking list.

Eliza West (24 disposals), Tamara Smith (20) and Jasmine Fleming (19) also shone for the Hawks, as did ruck Lucy Wales.

Isabelle Pritchard had match-high tallies of 31 disposals and eight clearances for the Bulldogs, with Elisabeth Georgostathis (19 disposals) also busy.

The Bulldogs kicked three of the first four goals but were held scoreless in the third quarter as the Hawks took control of the contest.

Meanwhile, Sunny Lappin kicked three goals and sparked the second-half surge that led to Gold Coast's 30-point win over Collingwood.

The Suns (3-2) kicked four goals to one in the third term — two of those to Lappin — to set up their 9.8 (62) to 4.8 (32) victory in Carrara.

Maddy Brancatisano kicked two goals, Charlie Rowbottom had 29 disposals and Dekota Baron provided the highlight of the day with a towering mark-of-the-year contender.

Mikayla Nurse suffered a nasty cut on the face after a head clash with Suns teammate Lucy Single late in the match.

Tarni White had 29 disposals for Collingwood (0-5), which remains winless this season.

AAP

World.title: Eels star Addo-Carr allegedly returns positive test for cocaine
World.content:
Star NRL player Josh Addo-Carr is being investigated by police after allegedly returning a positive test for cocaine.

Police confirmed in a statement that Addo-Carr was driving in Sydney's inner-west along Enmore Road last night when he was stopped for a random test.

He was subjected to a roadside breath test for alcohol, which returned a negative result.

However, he returned a preliminary drug wipe, which allegedly returned a positive indication for cocaine.

Josh Addo-Carr sacked from the Canterbury Bulldogs Josh Addo-Carr has been sacked by NRL club Canterbury with immediate effect after returning two positive readings to roadside drugs tests last month.

An oral fluid sample was obtained from Addo-Carr and sent for further analysis.

The investigation is ongoing, as police await the results of the forensic analysis.

His current club, the Parramatta Eels, released a statement noting it was aware of an alleged incident involving Addo-Carr.

"The club has notified the NRL Integrity unit and is cooperating with the appropriate processes, as well as providing welfare support to Josh and his family," the statement read.

The Parramatta Eels said it would not be commenting further until the matter was finalised.

In 2024, Addo-Carr was sacked from his previous club, the Canterbury Bulldogs, after he failed a roadside drug test.

Addo-Carr was recalled to the Australian national side, the Kangaroos, and has played for New South Wales.

Across his decade-long career, the winger has scored more than 150 tries and won two premierships with the Melbourne Storm.

The alleged positive test could affect Addo-Carr's chances of being selected for Australia for next month's World Cup.

Kangaroos coach Kevin Walters said Addo-Carr could face consequences if the allegation was verified.

"I had a lot to do with Josh last year on the Kangaroo tour," Walters told Fox League.

"He's a great team player, had a good series, but this may have some ramifications around that as well."

World.title: Antisemitism lawsuit dropped against former SBS newsreader
World.content:
A racial discrimination case against former SBS journalist Mary Kostakidis, over her social media posts about the Israel-Gaza war, has been discontinued.

The Zionist Federation of Australia’s (ZFA) chief executive Alon Cassuto launched the action in the Federal Court in South Australia last year, claiming the posts were "reasonably likely … to offend, insult, humiliate and/or intimidate Australian Jews".

However, the court yesterday ruled, with both parties' consent, that "the proceeding be discontinued with no order as to costs".

Zionist Federation of Australia chief executive Alon Cassuto launched the action in the Federal Court in South Australia last year. (ABC News)

Lawsuit's goal 'substantially satisfied'

In 2024, Ms Kostakidis shared a video on her X account of Hassan Nasrallah, the now-slain leader of Islamist militant group Hezbollah, urging Jews to leave Israel.

In the video, Nasrallah says "Israelis don't have a future" in the Middle East, and Ms Kostakidis captioned the post with: "The Israeli govt getting some of its own medicine".

The ZFA alleged the post was anti-Semitic under the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance’s definition, adopted by Australia, because it "denies the right of the Jewish people to self-determination".

Ms Kostakidis's lawyer argued the posts did not meet the "legal definition of anti-Semitism" and were "directed to the Israeli government" rather than Jews.

Supporters of former SBS newsreader Mary Kostakidis outside Adelaide's Federal Court building in July 2025. (ABC News)

In a statement, Mr Cassuto said he filed the lawsuit to "seek recognition of the harm these posts caused ordinary Jewish Australians", an objective that has been "substantially satisfied".

He acknowledged Ms Kostakidis apologised for any distress caused but said it "did not … mark a change in the character of [her] public commentary".

"I do not intend to spend another year taking Ms Kostakidis' repugnant commentary from the dark corners of the internet and giving it a Federal Court platform in her pursuit of martyrdom," Mr Cassuto said.

Kostakidis claims 'win for press freedom'

Ms Kostakidis described the outcome as a win for "freedom of political expression".

"I want to thank my fellow Australians who recognised the significance of what we stand to lose, stood with me and stepped up to assist me to launch my defence," she said.

"The purpose of journalism is to get to the truth — fearlessly — and to hold power to account. This is a win for press freedom, which has prevailed.

"Thank you to the Jewish and Israeli people all over the world raging against this in recognition our common humanity trumps any form of tribalism."

Ms Kostakidis presented SBS World News from 1987 to 2007, and has more recently been an outspoken critic of Israel.

World.title: Service Tasmania contact centre cuts will fuel digital divide, MP says
World.content:
A proposal to cut the operating hours of multiple Service Tasmania service centres by up to half has prompted concern for older residents.

The state government is proposing to reduce the opening hours of five Service Tasmania centres, due to a "reduction in foot traffic".

The changes would affect centres in the regional communities of Queenstown on the state's west coast, Oatlands and Campbell Town in the midlands, Currie on King Island, and Whitemark on Flinders Island — all of which already operate at reduced office hours.

The earmarked Service Tasmania centres are in regional locations, such as Queenstown. (ABC News: Maren Preuss)

Some residents 'really impacted', mayor says

Flinders Mayor Rachel Summers, who previously worked in customer service for Service Tasmania, said the proposal was concerning — particularly in an isolated region such as hers.

"We have a number of older people, a number of people who aren't able to access reliable internet services, and they're going to be really impacted by this decision," Councillor Summers said.

Rachel Summers says some residents in her community would be negatively impacted by the changes. (ABC News: Lucie Cutting)

The Flinders Island Service Tasmania service centre at Whitemark, the only one on the Bass Strait island, currently operates two days a week.

Under the proposed changes, its face-to-face operating hours would drop from 20 to 10 a week.

Cr Summers said additional restrictions on days and times would "further hamper" access, for a trip that is already a long distance for some residents.

She said while accessing services digitally could "absolutely work for some people", it would exclude others.

The state opposition has pledged to try to stop the changes. (ABC News: Kate Nickels)

"Government talk on forms and information sheets can be quite difficult to understand," Cr Summers said.

"If you're trying to get help with filling in a form, sometimes you actually need to be there in front of the person to see what they're writing, where they're writing.

" If you're checking that something's been filled in completely and accurately, you can't do that over the phone. "

Whitemark is the main administrative centre on Flinders Island. (ABC News: Kate Nickels)

Cr Summers said she expected the proposed changes would be discussed by the council.

The proposal was also criticised by the state opposition, which said contact hours would be "difficult to restore" once hours were cut.

"It's not like there's another shop that's just 10 minutes down the road for people that live on Flinders Island or King Island, for example," Bass MP Jess Greene said.

"We know that we have a digital divide in Tasmania.

'We know that these service cuts will have a negative impact on regional and our island communities.

"We're asking Premier Rockliff to reconsider these cuts."

The opening hour changes are open for public consultation from Monday. (ABC News: Kate Nickels)

Under the proposal, the reduced weekly operating hours would mean a cut from 25 hours to 20 hours in Oatlands, 32.5 hours to 16 hours in Queenstown, 25 to 16.5 hours in Campbell Town, and 20 to 10 hours in both Whitemark and Currie.

The state government has said no jobs would be lost, with "existing Service Tasmania staff in those regions to contribute remotely".

However, the ABC has seen a document outlining the proposal, which says the change will "reduce frontline staffing by approximately 1.9 FTE [full-time equivalent] in total across the five service centres".

"We will continue to monitor the impact of natural workforce attrition and assess future recruitment needs in line with ongoing service delivery needs," the document reads.

A government spokesperson said the 1.9 FTE positions referred to vacancies that "won't be filled across the whole Service Tasmania".

Usage behind decision, government says

Premier Jeremy Rockliff said the centres in question had been chosen following analysis of two years of customer visitation data, which found demand was much lower than the hours currently offered.

Where are the cuts coming from in Tasmania's state budget? Treasurer Eric Abetz wants to find $1.47 billion in "efficiencies" in Tasmania's state budget. This is what's on the chopping block.

"The way people access government services has changed significantly over recent years," Mr Rockliff said.

"As these customer preferences continue to evolve, it is important that we regularly review how services are delivered.

"We know many Tasmanians still rely on in-person services and that's why these changes have been proposed based on current customers' usage."

Consultation on the proposed changes, including which times and days would best meet local needs, will open on Monday and run until October 2.

World.title: World-first trial finds floating wetlands can cut greenhouse gas emissions
World.content:
Researchers believe a floating garden of native plants on a wastewater lagoon in VIctoria's east could help tackle greenhouse gas emissions, after it cut the lagoon's emissions by about 30 per cent.

The floating wetland is part of a world-first study conducted by RMIT University, Westernport Water and the CSIRO on Phillip Island over two years.

The 330-square-metre platform, roughly the size of one-and-a-half tennis courts, was planted with native reeds and sedges, with their roots hanging into the wastewater below.

RMIT's Centre for Nature Positive Solutions research fellow Lukas Schuster said the plants' roots created habitat for microbes that could help break down organic matter and absorb nutrients and pollutants.

"Floating wetlands are, you can imagine, like buoyant platforms that basically have the wetland plants planted onto them and the roots are hanging down into the water," Dr Schuster said.

Lukas Schuster says the trial's scale was important in testing whether floating wetlands could work in a real-world wastewater treatment setting. (Supplied: RMIT)

"So they're made to clean the water basically."

Researchers found the floating wetland reduced carbon dioxide emissions by up to 36 per cent, methane by up to 66 per cent and nitrogen by 18 per cent compared with a control lagoon without a wetland.

Dr Schuster said wastewater treatment was a significant source of emissions globally.

"On a global scale, they produce roughly 700 million tonnes of greenhouse gases every year," he said.

The world-first trial by RMIT University, Westernport Water and CSIRO has found a floating wetland cuts emissions from a wastewater lagoon by about 30 per cent on average. (Supplied: RMIT)

"Now we think about Victoria alone, for example, that is roughly one million tonnes of greenhouse gases every year.

"And so reducing those emissions is very tricky, but it's a very important step that we show basically that we can reduce emissions in open lagoons."'

The lagoon contained about 14 million litres of wastewater, with emissions monitored continuously over two years using solar-powered sensors.

Lukas Schuster says floating wetlands are like "buoyant platforms", with roots hanging down into the lagoons. (Supplied: RMIT)

Years of research

Dr Schuster said the trial's scale was important in testing whether floating wetlands could work in a real-world wastewater treatment setting.

"We were basically measuring the greenhouse gas emissions continuously; we were there every month deploying sensors and measuring the emissions continuously across the two years," he said.

Researchers say the technology could be useful because floating wetlands could potentially be retrofitted into existing lagoons without major infrastructure changes.

The floating wetlands hold a number of plants that assist in cutting greenhouse gas emissions from the lagoons. (Supplied: RMIT)

Dr Schuster said water companies had already expressed interest in further trials.

"It's also not only emission reduction, but also pollutant removal," he said.

"We're talking about perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) removal or other pollutants in the wastewater and also maybe provide habitat for biodiversity."

Dams to be trialled next

Researchers are now trialling similar floating wetlands in farm dams across the Bass Coast, investigating their potential to improve water quality, biodiversity and emissions.

An aerial view of a floating wetland in a Bass Coast farm dam as part of another ongoing trial, where researchers are exploring the potential benefits. (Supplied: RMIT)

Dr Schuster said future research would also look at making the floating platforms more sustainable, including through recycled or plant-based materials.

"It will also be super interesting to see whether we can make them a bit more sustainable," he said.

"For example, like with recycled materials or plant-based materials rather than having actually plastic-based baskets, for the floating wetland."

Benefits for farmers

Kernot farmer Camilla Graves has floating wetlands in two of her 26 farm dams as part of the trial.

"Dams are essential, and one thing we have been concerned about is actually the quality of the water in our dams," Ms Graves said.

She said the floating wetlands also provide protection to ducks, which use dams for habitat, from predators.

Camilla Graves has two dams that are being used to test floating wetlands. (Supplied: RMIT)

"The floating wetlands have actually provided an opportunity for them to take some shelter where the foxes can't get to them because the floating wetland literally is in the middle of the dam," Ms Graves said.

She said people who were not from regional Victoria may not realise how dependent nearby agricultural communities are on water collected and stored on farms.

"Water quality is really prime to agriculture," Ms Graves said.

She said the floating wetlands could be easily adopted by other farmers.

"Its simplicity is amazing; this concept can definitely be rolled out Australia-wide to farmers that are interested in giving it a go," Ms Grave said.

World.title: Live: Dolphins claim historic finals win, Sharks and Cowboys play for survival
World.content:
— reporting by AAP

The Dolphins are through to their first preliminary final after strike centre Herbie Farnworth ignited a stunning 26-16 comeback win over the Warriors in Auckland.

The Warriors appeared on track for victory when 16-8 ahead with 20 minutes remaining, but the Dolphins have been comeback specialists in 2026 and the electric Farnworth danced and weaved his way through to score.

A 90m movement, started and finished by Dolphins fullback Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow via a scintillating interchange of passing with Farnworth, put the Dolphins ahead 20-16.

Then Dolphins centre Jack Bostock iced the win with a ball steal to score and secure the Dolphins a home preliminary final at Lang Park in a fortnight.

A sold-out crowd of 26,131 at Mt Smart Stadium was pulsating and heaving throughout another classic battle between two sides that are fast forging a fierce rivalry.

They were silenced in the final 20 minutes by a Dolphins side that refused to be beaten.

The Warriors will now host Newcastle in a semifinal next week.

This showdown was brutal, physical, fast and furious.

Warriors pair Adam Pompey and Kurt Capewell, along with Dolphins winger Selwyn Cobbo, were all sent to the sin-bin in the first half.

Dolphins prop Thomas Flegler was concussed and ruled out of the match in the 10th minute after being steamrolled by opposite front-rower Mitch Barnett.

Pompey and Dolphins trio Isaiya Katoa, Connelly Lemuelu and Kodi Nikorima were all put on report as the clash boiled.

The match exploded into a melee in the 34th minute after Dolphins half Isaiya Katoa accidentally flipped Warriors prop Jackson Ford in a dangerous tackle.

Capewell and Cobbo were both sin-binned for rushing in to the fracas and Katoa was put on report.

The Warriors suffered a major blow with strike centre Leka Halasima ruled out in the warm-up after clutching at his right hamstring, with Pompey slotting into the starting side..

Every penalty or ruck infringement in the Warriors' favour was met with an almighty roar by the crowd.

The Warriors faithful were delirious when fullback Taine Tuaupiki danced past four Dolphins to score under the sticks.

At 10-2 the Warriors were in control.

Farnworth came into the match with nine tries in seven matches against the Warriors but it was the Englishman's masterful tip-on to Cobbo that got the visitors their first try.

Pompey was sin-binned for a shoulder charge on Dolphins warhorse Ray Stone.

Tuaupiki kept landing penalty goals but the Dolphins scored the tries that sealed the deal.

World.title: NRL finals LIVE: Sharks open scoring against Cowboys in sudden-death finals clash
World.content:
North Queensland desperately need to find consistency in their game. And I don’t necessarily mean from week-to-week, I mean from one set to the next. The Cowboys’ strength is their right-side attack and they’ll ask plenty of questions of Cronulla, but their own defence is a real issue too – 41.5 missed tackles ranks them 16th in the NRL for the season.

For the Sharks, it’s the same question every year as they limp into the finals with one win from their last five games. Have they got another gear? Personally, I don’t think so, I think the Cowboys have got an upset in them.

Time to step up: All eyes are on Braydon Trindall returning from injury but for me, it’s Nicho Hynes who needs to fire. He needs to own the result. That’s the responsibility that comes with being the highest-paid player at your club and a marquee player.

Scott Drinkwater is North Queensland’s most creative player when he jumps into the front line. They’re all-in on him – good, bad, rocks or diamonds, that’s just how he plays.

World.title: ‘Spitting, kicking, headbutting’: Two men arrested after violent threats aboard flight
World.content:
NationalVictoriaCrime ‘Spitting, kicking, headbutting’: Two men arrested after violent threats aboard flight James Costa September 12, 2026 — 7:32pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Two men were restrained on a flight from Melbourne to Doha after making violent threats towards passengers and crew, including claiming they had a gun, and allegedly assaulting staff members. The men were arrested by Qatari authorities upon arrival in Doha on Friday night, Qatar Airways said in a statement. Loading The men appeared “extremely agitated and restless” from the moment they boarded the aircraft, a woman on the flight, who wished to remain anonymous, said. “They were repeatedly getting in and out of their seats, moving around the cabin and into my personal space, and touching or moving my belongings,” she said.



“They were also repeatedly rummaging through their luggage and saying they were looking for items they had apparently misplaced.” Things escalated about six hours before the plane was set to land, when the two men, who the woman said were brothers, began arguing and then fighting. “The men would not comply with instructions from the crew, and ultimately had to be restrained,” the woman said. The men made threats about using a gun and killing people, according to the woman.



A passenger immediately stepped in and restrained one of the brothers, while cabin crew members restrained the other. One of the men remained “extremely angry and agitated – he was yelling, spitting, kicking and headbutting a flight attendant”. “Several male passengers stepped forward to assist the cabin crew in restraining him, and I have to commend those passengers. “They were absolutely amazing and showed enormous courage in helping the crew and protecting other passengers.” The woman also said that the cabin crew deserved credit for handling the difficult and frightening situation professionally, and doing “everything they possibly could to calm the situation and protect the other passengers”.



Virgin Australia said that the flight was operated by Qatar Airways, which said in a statement that “two male passengers were involved in a physical altercation on board flight VA7 from Melbourne to Doha, operated by Qatar Airways”. Related Article Crime ‘A gun, knives and a can of fuel’: Passengers recount terrifying moment when armed teen boarded flight “Both passengers were restrained and, upon arrival in Doha, were handed over to local authorities.” “The safety and wellbeing of our crew and passengers remain our highest priority.” Damien Ractliffe, who was at the front of the plane and did not see the incident, said he saw uniformed men board the plane when it landed in Doha.



“[The] only thing [I] would love to understand is if these people are coming back into Australia,” a passenger told 3AW’s Jacqui Felgate. “Given the language they were screaming about wanting to hurt and shoot people, they really shouldn’t be allowed back in,” they said. The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade did not, last night, confirm whether the men were Australian citizens. Be the first to know when major news happens.

World.title: Dolphins into NRL’s final four with comeback win over Warriors
World.content:
Warriors 16 Dolphins 26 SportNRLNRL 2026 Dolphins into NRL’s final four with comeback win over Warriors Chris Barrett Updated September 12, 2026 — 7:18pm ,first published 6:33pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

For nearly four decades Brisbane has been the Broncos’ turf, a status earned with seven premierships and a galaxy of stars. On the penultimate weekend of this season, however, Suncorp Stadium will be painted red and white. Loading The new kids on the block, the Dolphins, are the toast of the town, booking a home preliminary final with a come-from-behind 26-16 victory over the New Zealand Warriors at Go Media Stadium in Auckland. The club has a long and rich history in Brisbane suburban football stretching back to 1947, but the NRL iteration is in its infancy and this was its finest hour to date.



In their first finals match, the Dolphins trailed 16-8 with 20 minutes remaining in what to that point had been an old-school battle of attrition featuring six penalty goals – five of them to the Warriors – and three sin-binnings. But they stormed home with tries to Herbie Farnworth, Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow and Jack Bostock to move to within just one match of a title decider in only their fourth season in the league. Loading “It’s one of those things you can’t describe what it means. It’s obviously massive for everyone involved at the club,” Dolphins coach Kristian Woolf said. “The club has done such a good job over four years. “The blokes who deserve the credit are the players. The way they played tonight, they bravery they showed under pressure, they’ve done that so many times at the back end of the season ... They’re in this position for a reason and that’s because they want to work hard and they want to work hard for each other.”



While the Dolphins will have the week off before their grand final qualifier, the Warriors will be forced to take the long route in the finals, starting with a sudden-death showdown against Newcastle next weekend. Farnworth and Bostock stood up when it counted in the four-tries-to-one triumph while a hitherto quiet Tabuai-Fidow also shot to life in the closing stages to put the visitors in front with an end-to-end try. Stung by the defeat, the Warriors could also again be without Jackson Ford against the Knights after he injured his ankle in his return from a torn pectoral muscle. They had also suffered an unexpected blow before play when Leka Halamisa strained a hamstring in the warm-up and was scratched. Amid the disappointment, Warriors coach Andrew Webster was putting on a brave face.



“I don’t think we can sulk for long. There’s another path for us,” Webster said. “It’s not the direct path, it’s going to be a different one. We’ve got to move on quick.” Dolphins players celebrate in the dying stages. Getty Images The Dolphins had been left a man down soon after kick-off when Thomas Flegler’s head connected with Mitch Barnett’s hip in a tackle and he was ruled out with concussion. There followed a procession of players off the field for reasons other than injury and interchange in a highly charged first half.



First, Halasima’s last-minute replacement Adam Pompey was sin-binned for a shoulder charge on Ray Stone, then Kurt Capewell and Selwyn Cobbo were each marched for 10 minutes for running to join a melee. Related Article Live

NRL 2026 NRL finals LIVE: Sharks open scoring against Cowboys in sudden-death finals clash That briefly left the Warriors with 11 versus 12 but they still managed to take a 12-8 lead to the break courtesy of Taine Tuaupiki, who spun and stepped beyond four defenders to score a fabulous individual try and booted three penalty goals. Webster’s side had leaked 88 points in the past three weeks but held their line desperately to restrict the Dolphins to a sole try to Cobbo, set up with a deft catch and pass from Farnworth. The Dolphins might have lost another to the sin bin 10 minutes after play resumed but Connelly Lemuelu escaped with going on report for a hip-drop tackle on Ali Leiataua.



They slipped further behind with two more Tuaupiki goals. The stage was set for a thrilling finale just after the hour, however, when Farnworth scooped up a bouncing ball and swerved between three tacklers to cross the line. Six minutes later Tabuai-Fidow burst into action, racing clear from deep in the Dolphins’ territory before linking with Farnworth to hit the lead. Bostock’s opportunistic steal with five minutes on the clock clinched the late ambush. Webster defended his side repeatedly opting to take the two points rather than pushing for more.



He said if the Warriors had declined the shots and goal and “got beaten by two, I probably would have got sacked”. “To go up by eight points is a no-brainer, you’ve got to do it,” Webster said. In the end, it wasn’t enough.

World.title: Baker colts show class at three to put group 1 targets on radar
World.content:
SportRacingHorse racing Baker colts show class at three to put group 1 targets on radar Craig Kerry September 12, 2026 — 7:09pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Warwoven tuned up for target race the Golden Rose and Paradoxium put his hand up for an Everest slot as Warwick Farm trainer Bjorn Baker celebrated a group race interstate double with his three-year-old colts on Saturday. Stakes winners at two despite setback in their campaigns, the pair starred with commanding victories on Saturday as Warwoven claimed the group 2 Run To The Rose (1200m) at Rosehill and Paradoxium led all the way in the group 3 Poseidon Stakes (1100m) at Flemington. Rachel King salutes on Warwoven in the Run To The Rose. Getty Images Rachel King put Warwoven ($8), the Pago Pago Stakes winner, outside leader Castillo King from gate seven of 11, and he travelled well before holding out favourite St Gotthard by a neck. Under Focus was third. It was a bounce-back performance from Warwoven, which was three lengths fifth first-up in the San Domenico Stakes (1100m) in Guest House’s track-record time win at Rosehill.



Baker assistant trainer Luke Hilton said the group 1 Golden Rose (1400m) in two weeks was always the target for Warwoven, which had come back bigger and stronger this preparation. He was $11 into $6 for the Golden Rose, where Guest House was a $2.80 favourite. “We knew he was going really well,” Hilton said. “We were still a little bit disappointed first up, but when you sort of sat back and looked at it in isolation, he had gone really well. “Rachel was very confident and very happy that he’d gone well, and he’d just come on from that run. “He’s got good early speed when he needs it, and I like what Bjorn did with him first up because the idea was always to go to 1400. “We wanted to make sure that he could take a sit and be restrained, which he sort of adapted to pretty well first up. So now we’re there with one to go.”



Earlier in the day, Paradoxium put its case forward for Yulong’s Everest slot with a front-running victory first-up at Flemington. The Extreme Choice colt, bought by Yulong in March, controlled the straight race under Jason Collett and powered away late for a one-length win to add to his group 2 Todman Stakes success. Baker was bullish about his chance leading into the run. “He’s got a great attitude and a great action,” Baker said. “Speaking pre-race, I did everything but declare him. “He was very good and he had to carry a little bit more weight than the others as well. Hopefully we can get back here for the Coolmore [Stud Stakes]. You dream, and you dream big.”



Hilton said Paradoxium would return home for the Roman Consul Stakes before heading back down for the Coolmore. As for the Everest, he said: “Paradoxium is obviously Yulong and they have a slot, so they might want to be in discussions, but we haven’t really floated it about this bloke [Warwoven].” Payne on a roll for three-year-olds Veteran Rosehill trainer David Payne was looking to a fourth consecutive week of wins with exciting three-year-olds after Persian Wonder sliced through late to win the group 3 Ming Dynasty Quality (1400m) earlier in the day. Persian Wonder, a $19 chance after finishing fifth in the group 3 Up And Coming Stakes, finished through the pack under Ash Morgan after the leaders set a solid tempo.



It continued a dream run for Payne, who won a Midway with VRC Derby hope Proxima Dea two weeks ago before Bangkok Hottie took out the group 2 Furious Stakes last week. He will have Bangkok Hottie and Krasina in next week’s group 2 Tea Rose Stakes (1400m) for the fillies at Randwick. “It makes me feel a bit younger. It’s nice. I’ve found three good ones,” said Payne, who was surprised at Persian Wonder’s big odds. “It was wonderful run [last start], and he’s dropped three kilos against Genesis Runner and that, but people don’t see that. He got beat two lengths by them, and he had to come wide.” Payne said Persian Wonder, which had one win in nine starts before Saturday, had shown promise from the start but was “just a big dumb-dumb” early days. He said the group 3 Gloaming Stakes (1800m) on October 10 was a next target before a potential shot at the group Spring Champion (2000m). “He’s not bred to get a trip but everybody who rides him says he’ll stay a trip, so we’ll go to the Gloaming,” Payne said.



“Then maybe the Spring Champion, if he stays.” As for Persian Wonder beating some high-priced opposition, Payne said: “He’s expensive, he cost $160,000. For me, that’s expensive.” Savvy return puts Everest in the frame Hawkesbury trainer Brad Widdup has the group 1 Manikato Stakes as the next step for comeback mare Savvy Hallie, but he said the Everest is in the picture after she led all the way to claim the group 2 Sheraco Stakes (1200m) at Rosehill. A $20 chance after finishing last first-up in the Toy Show Quality and being deemed one-fifth lame by stewards, Savvy Hallie was taken to the front by Nash Rawiller from gate seven of eight to take control of the mares’ race.



Nash Rawiller wins the Sheraco Stakes on Savvy Hallie. Getty Images She was strong late to hold out Gangsta Granny by a neck, with favourite Lazzura another half-neck away in third. Widdup is the head trainer for Everest slot-holders Mulberry Racing, which had its own horse, Jedibeel, in the $20 million race last year. Although not owned by Mulberry, Savvy Hallie now appears in the mix for the slot. “It’s in discussions,” Widdup said. “The other one is Headwall, and it was very good the other day, he’s a very good horse, but it’s in discussions.” Widdup said the goal was to get a group 1 win with the four-year-old, which was a close second to Tempted in last year’s Surround Stakes, and the September 27 Manikato at Caulfield was a likely target.



“Nothing went right first-up and that’s her at her best there today,” he said. “She has done it before. We took her to the Gold Coast and I thought she was terribly hard to beat there and she was flat, ran fourth. “Then first-up the other day, she didn’t get slammed out of the gates, so went back to the inside. It was a no-go zone and other things, like apparently she was lame, but she’s not lame today. Not a thing wrong with her and she’s proved that today.” Skyhook rocks in opening act to Eagle Co-trainer Sterling Alexiou was eyeing potentially just one more run before the $10 million Golden Eagle (1500m) on October 31 for Skyhook after he returned with an impressive win in the group 2 Theo Marks (1300m) at Rosehill. Backed into a $2 favourite despite drawing the outside gate, Skyhook found the one-one under Kerrin McEvoy before surging to a length and a quarter win.



Alexiou, who trains in partnership with Gerald Ryan, said the Shannon Stakes, Alan Brown Stakes or the Silver Eagle were all possible races for the entire leading into the Golden Eagle. “He’s a pretty athletic horse, he doesn’t cop a lot of work,” said Alexiou, who ruled out an Epsom run. “We could have just one more run and it wouldn’t worry us. “After his last-start win in Queensland [the Gunsynd in June], we basically worked backwards from the Golden Eagle, how we thought we could get him there in his best form.” He said Skyhook had come of age since his Queensland winter campaign. “I just think he lacked a bit of strength in prior preparations. He could do it at both end but he’s just an older horse now and he learned to absorb a bit more race pressure and sustain it at both ends,” he said.



Sheza Alibi, a brilliant winner of the Makybe Diva Stakes on Saturday, is also headed to the Golden Eagle. “You never run away from one horse,” Alexiou said. “It’s been our aim for five months now.” Doyle gets in early for double delight The early booking of premier jockey James McDonald paid off for Formal ($7.50), which prevailed as the longest-priced of Nathan Doyle’s three runners in the Midway Handicap as part of a double for the Newcastle trainer. Formal run down stablemate Better Late ($4) by three-quarters of a length in the 1200m for his first Saturday city win. The five-year-old was a $27,500 buy for Calibre Racing.



“That’s how he had to ride him, he’s been getting too far back. He will sustain, but he won’t sprint five or six lengths and pick them up,” Doyle said. “I booked [McDonald] a couple of weeks ago. [Manager Mark Guest] asked if I had a horse in the Midway and that was the only one at that stage.” Doyle said Formal was likely to go for a spell and return in the summer. Doyle later won the benchmark 78 handicap (1500m) with another former Godolphin galloper, seven-year-old Silvanito. Baker-trained staying prospect Appeared could also be headed for a break soon after the Darby-bought import made it three from three in Australia. The five-year-old backed up wins at Newcastle and Warwick Farm, kicking clear late to take out the 2400m benchmark 78 handicap by two lengths.



Hilton said there was likely not much left this preparation for Appeared, which they wanted to give a foundation ahead of an autumn campaign. Wayburn gave a recovering Matt Dunn his 50th Highway Handicap victory a week later than needed, dominating the 1400m class 3 at Rosehill on Saturday by two lengths under apprentice Mollie Fitzgerald. Dunn, resting at home after knee surgery following an e-bike accident, gained slots for Band Of Brothers ($4.50) and Considered ($11) in the $2 million Kosciuszko during the week, but he also had hopes for Wayburn, which was unlucky when sixth a week earlier in a 1200m Highway. Stable representative Holly Julius said, with all slots now filled, Wayburn could go for a spell. Dunn is the first trainer to reach 50 wins in the Saturday country-only races.

World.title: Corruption watchdog charges police officer over alleged pepper spray assault
World.content:
NationalVictoriaCourts Corruption watchdog charges police officer over alleged pepper spray assault Cameron Houston September 12, 2026 — 7:00pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

A Victoria police officer has been charged by the state’s corruption watchdog with assaulting and falsely imprisoning a teenager, who is also suing the officer in the state’s Supreme Court. Constable Mitchell Andrews was charged in July with false imprisonment and common law assault by the Independent Broad-based Anti-corruption Commission, following an investigation known as Operation Yew. A Victoria Police constable has been charged with using excessive force. Paul Rovere The alleged victim, Jaimi Cook, who was 17 at the time of his interaction with Andrews, has filed a statement of claim with the Supreme Court and will pursue damages from the Victorian government. Cook was one of six teenagers Andrews told to line up and provide their names, after security staff at Westfield Knox Shopping Centre asked police to remove the group from a playground in May 2024.



However, Cook refused to give his name. He said: “don’t f---ing touch me” when Andrews allegedly attempted to stop him from walking away, according to court documents. Related Article Exclusive

Victoria Police conduct ‘We’re hog-tying’: Gippsland police accused of repeat misconduct after one victim suffers brain damage The teenager alleges Andrews grabbed him by the right arm while another officer placed him in a headlock, before he was taken to the ground. “The police officers continued to forcefully apply pressure to the plaintiff’s body as he wriggled in pain and told the police officers to let go of him. Officer Andrews then sprayed the plaintiff in the face with his police-issued

oleoresin capsicum spray,” according to the statement of claim. While pinned to the ground and placed in handcuffs, Cook insisted he had done nothing wrong, but eventually provided his name to officers and asked them to notify his mother.



A check of the LEAP database revealed Cook had no criminal history and no interactions with police, but a search of his bag found he was in possession of a small quantity of cannabis and magic mushrooms. He was taken to Knox police station and later charged with two counts of possessing a drug of dependence and two counts of resisting an emergency worker on duty. But all charges were withdrawn at a hearing in a children’s court in February last year. Cook, now 19, told The Age he had suffered from panic attacks and depression since the alleged assault. “It’s basically just made me shut out from the world. I’m too scared to go outside, or even to the city, or any place where there could be a police presence,” he said. Cook’s lawyer, Jeremy King from Robinson Gill Lawyers, alleges in court documents that police did not have a lawful basis to detain his client or reasonable grounds to arrest him, while the search of his backpack was also unlawful.



King, according to the statement of claim, will pursue general damages for the injuries and medical costs incurred by his client, but will also seek aggravated damages based on the alleged police misconduct. Related Article Courts Police cleared of manslaughter over man’s traffic arrest death “The conduct constituting the batteries, separately and as a course of conduct perpetrated by the police officers in concert was a violent and inexcusable abuse of authority, perpetrated in a manner designed to increase the plaintiff’s pain, humiliation and suffering,” according to the statement of claim. The officers involved in Cook’s arrest are also accused of making false statements to cover their tracks. “The police officers prepared, and relied upon, statements that were misleading in material respects and sought to inaccurately and retrospectively justify the plaintiff’s unlawful arrest and the excessive use of force upon him,” according to documents filed with the court.



Related Article Opinion

Victoria Police conduct Police are being asked to mark their own homework. No wonder they’re getting good grades Nadia Morales CEO of Inner Melbourne Community Legal A Victoria Police spokeswoman declined to comment while the matter was before the courts. King also declined to comment on the case. IBAC previously released a statement confirming it had charged Andrews with two offences. “Operation Yew was established by IBAC’s Focused Police Complaints Team, who assess and investigate serious single-incident complaints about Victoria Police by those at a higher risk of experiencing police misconduct, including children and young people. “As the matter is now before the court, no further information is available,” says the IBAC statement.



Last week, IBAC announced another officer had been charged over the alleged assault of a teenager during an arrest in Braybrook in October 2025. The leading senior constable was charged with two counts of aggravated assault with a weapon and two counts of unlawful assault, following a separate investigation known as Operation Bunya. “It is alleged that the Leading Senior Constable unlawfully struck the teen with a baton multiple times and stood on the teenager while they were being restrained on the ground,” according to a statement from IBAC. World.title: Melbourne’s newest cabaret venue used to be toilet paper storage
World.content:
NationalVictoriaCity life Melbourne’s newest cabaret venue used to be toilet paper storage Cara Waters September 12, 2026 — 7:00pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Filled with boxes of toilet paper, Christmas decorations and filing cabinets, the room on the top floor of the Melbourne Recital Centre sat neglected for 17 years. But philanthropists Peter and Ruth McMullin saw the potential in the hidden storage space, which has been transformed into a venue for cabaret, jazz, contemporary music and musical theatre. Philanthropists Ruth and Peter McMullin in the former storage space at the Melbourne Recital Centre. Jason South “For the first 17 years of the centre it’s just been a fairly dormant junkyard,” Melbourne Recital Centre chief executive Sandra Willis says. The McMullins donated $1 million, which was matched by the Victorian government’s $1 million to turn the storage space into an intimate performance venue.



The toilet paper is gone and, in its place is a bar, a grand piano positioned in front of geometric windows looking out over the city skyline and blue velvet fringed booths for seating. Related Article Exclusive

City life As music venues continue to shut, this Melbourne icon is hitting its high note The Peter and Ruth McMullin Beacon will host its first public performances on September 17, with international cabaret performer and “Melbourne gal” Meow Meow opening the venue across three nights. Willis says at a time when small music venues are struggling across Melbourne the opening of the Beacon offers new opportunities for artists. “We’ve seen so many small live music venues shut down, not reopen after COVID, or reopened and have struggled,” Willis says. “It’s been a theme that unfortunately has been going on with live music venues ever since pokies really.”



Willis says the closure of The Butterfly Club last year had a big impact on opportunities for artists in Melbourne as the venue used to host cabaret and indie performances. “This is part of our answer at Melbourne Recital Centre that we can provide a space for that artist that perhaps wouldn’t necessarily always perform in the Elisabeth Murdoch Hall to 1000 people,” she says. “Instead a small space like this will be a really intimate performance.” Meow Meow performing at a preview performance at The Beacon. Laura Manariti Willis says opening the Beacon also allows the Melbourne Recital Centre to attract a new type of audience. “We want to reshape what the word recital means,” she says. “It’s often considered that it might be something that only a classical Western canon chamber music, and actually a recital can be all sorts of ways of storytelling, all sorts of different music forms. One unplugged artist performing on a guitar is a recital.”



Peter McMullin, the son of Spotless founder Ian McMullin and a former deputy mayor of Melbourne, is a prolific philanthropist alongside his wife Ruth. The couple donated $4 million to the University of Melbourne’s science gallery and established the Centre for Statelessness within the Melbourne Law School. McMullin says his motivation for backing the creation of the Beacon is quite personal. “My first legal practice in Smith Street, Collingwood, used to be next to the Last Laugh, which was on the corner of Gertrude and Smith street, and we used to go there after work,” he says. “I probably spent too long there, but all the emerging artists – comedians, musicians – used to perform up there, and it was fantastic.” He gazes around the completed venue with its reflective ceiling and large spectrogram artwork lining the walls with pride.



“I reckon it beats the Lincoln Centre in New York – but I would say that, wouldn’t I?” Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.

World.title: History shows where new technology can lead
World.content:
Letters NationalVictoriaLetters History shows where new technology can lead September 12, 2026 — 8:00pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Photo: Matt Golding To submit a letter to The Age, email letters@theage.com.au. Please include your home address and telephone number. No attachments, please include your letter in the body of the email. See here for our rules and tips on getting your letter published. Echoes of the past

It is extremely disturbing to hear former workers at Anthropic warn of the impact artificial intelligence may have on the future of humanity (“Anthropic insiders stunning AI warning”, 11/9). AI technology systems could develop an independent power of their own, subsequently out of the control of humans.

I am reminded of the splitting of the atom that developed into nuclear power and nuclear weapons (the atomic bomb that devastated Hiroshima) and continue to pose a constant threat to civilisation. The development of AI is proceeding so fast that political leadership seems unable to grasp the magnitude of its potential danger, while a few individuals make billions of dollars.

Judith Morrison, Nunawading Sword of Damocles

Human inventions are a double-edged sword. The Anthropic article reports that artificial super-intelligence, is capable of killing us all in a decade. Toxic pesticides, efficient factory robots and sophisticated weapons, originally considered beneficial, are projected to eventually contribute to our demise too. I’m not sure how any individual or social intervention can prevent these things happening. Nevertheless, the other side of the sword could be a more pristine environment due to human extinction – what the Earth’s other inhabitants yearn for.

Andrew Smith, Leongatha Burbling along

Your correspondent (Letters, 10/9) is right re postcode snobbery. More examples include parts of Moorabbin changing to Hampton East or Bentleigh East (which used to be East Bentleigh), Cheltenham to Pennydale, Gardenvale to Brighton and East Brighton to Brighton East (except hopefully on my Age letters!).

Samantha Keir, East Brighton



Keep to ourselves

Australia should not need a crystal ball or Kevin Rudd’s undoubted expertise to predict the inevitability of China’s takeover of Taiwan (“Rudd warns nation on borrowed time”, 11/9). The likelihood of a takeover, peaceful or not, has always been a question not of whether, but when, and there is frustratingly little anyone can do about it. Turning a blind eye will not work any better than appeasement or resistance. Australia will be wise to get its own house in order and not seek to interfere in other people’s problems.

Jenifer Nicholls, Windsor Sky is not falling

Let’s look at the maths behind the overblown rhetoric that is coming from certain politicians. “The sky is falling with a supposed 10 per cent drop in the housing market.” That market has risen 2300 per cent to 2600 per cent in the past 50 years. Let that sink in. If there is a 10 per cent fall that would only bring house prices back to 2024 prices – and they were overblown then. Too much scaremongering and less proper analysis is being done by people who have vested interest in creating disruption.

Greg Tuck, Warragul Symbolism is a start

Your correspondent (Letters, 11/9) uses deflection to avoid the legitimate point Ed Miliband is making (Israel blasts UK’s West Bank stance″⁣, 10/9). Rightful individual owners of land, which has been in their hands for generations, are being threatened with the intention of forcing them off that land.

The Israeli Defence Force is doing little or nothing to protect them. So who is going to come to their aid? In these circumstances the UK is right to impose sanctions on illegal settlers – even if they achieve little. This action may be symbolic but at least it’s a start.

Ivan Glynn, Vermont Problem, no solution

Columnist Jenna Price and your correspondents (Letters, 11/9) rightly point out that far too many parents appear to leave too much of the teaching of proper behaviour to school teachers.

They, however, do not address the main problem that some parents are simply not cut out for the task. Some lack the necessary skills, some lack the required interest and others are just too busy. Asking parents to do better will almost certainly go unheeded by many of those most in need.

Although perhaps a harsh judgment, it is a simple fact that nearly everyone is capable of producing children. Regrettably, some people shouldn’t.

In other words, we seem to have an intractable problem with no solution in sight.

Al Morris, Doncaster The time factor

Once I was approached by an angry father with the words: “You want to call yourself a teacher, and you cannot even control my kid!” I was very upset, having not taught long at this stage. I asked my principal for advice. He asked, how long per week do you teach the student? Two hours a week! How long is he with his parents?

I was reconciled. Still teaching and loving it.

Luise Mock, Tawonga South



Fertility not a factor

In a parent-teacher meeting I explained how the student in question’s behaviour towards his peers, especially females, could improve. Aggressive response, “Do you have children?” As it happens, I did not and could not. Was told, “I thought not.”

I have several teaching and other qualifications, but was not told on entering any of the courses that fertility was a prerequisite.

Rosalind McIntosh, Camberwell Howard’s way to war

It seems John Howard has conveniently forgotten he sent troops into the folly of Iraq on the false premise of weapons of mass destruction. Iraq and Saddam Hussein had nothing to do with 9/11 and he ignored the intelligence that stated Hussein was not a threat.

Ross Hosking, Blackwood, SA Climate for change

Amid the distraction of outrage and u-turns from One Nation and the muddle of the Coalition, the government gives away more of our gas and gives way on our climate (“Labor softens gas export rules to calm Asian buyers”, 11/9).

The government claims it is helping our Asian neighbours. It is not. More gas for export helps the gas companies make more money, that’s all.

More action on climate will help our Asian neighbours. In a warming climate, these regions will be among the first to become unliveable. There is an urgent need for more Independents and Greens in parliament, to keep our climate on the agenda, as the major parties seem to have lost interest.

Jenny Kashyap, Bentleigh Source the cash, Trump

Missing from the discussion re President Donald Trump’s offer to pay every US citizen $5000 is the vital unanswered question: Where is the money coming from? What other government services will be slashed to fulfil his outrageous bribe?

Meg Paul, Camberwell See you next time, NFL

The San Francisco 49ers – They came, they saw, they conquered. They spent a full week acclimatising, were generous with their time among the public, and made many fans. The Los Angeles Rams chose to fly in about 25 hours before game time. They were soundly beaten 27-7. They flew out. It was a wonderful event for Melbourne and was an overwhelming success. I still don’t understand the game, but hope it returns next year.

Geoff Lipton, Caulfield North Don’t bother, NFL

America’s NFL conquered Melbourne with over 100,000 spectators at the MCG. Unfortunately, the game was basically boring with a few flashes of excitement. On the other side of Australia, Fremantle and Geelong put on a game that had fans excited and involved from the start to the finish. Long may Aussie Rules survive.

Peter Roche, Carlton

World.title: NRL finals LIVE: Sharks open scoring against Cowboys in sudden-death finals clash
World.content:
North Queensland desperately need to find consistency in their game. And I don’t necessarily mean from week-to-week, I mean from one set to the next. The Cowboys’ strength is their right-side attack and they’ll ask plenty of questions of Cronulla, but their own defence is a real issue too – 41.5 missed tackles ranks them 16th in the NRL for the season.

For the Sharks, it’s the same question every year as they limp into the finals with one win from their last five games. Have they got another gear? Personally, I don’t think so, I think the Cowboys have got an upset in them.

Time to step up: All eyes are on Braydon Trindall returning from injury but for me, it’s Nicho Hynes who needs to fire. He needs to own the result. That’s the responsibility that comes with being the highest-paid player at your club and a marquee player.

Scott Drinkwater is North Queensland’s most creative player when he jumps into the front line. They’re all-in on him – good, bad, rocks or diamonds, that’s just how he plays.
